  flipped back to `true` between one session's explicit disable and the next
  session's unrelated check, source unconfirmed. A rerender dispatched from an
  in-flight job reads its OWN snapshot of `content_data`/`sections` at claim
  time, the same way `orchestration_states.workflow_plan` does for council
  runs (see the other in-flight-snapshot landmine) — so a DB fix you make
  *after* a rerender has already started will not be seen by that run, and its
  output can arrive and overwrite your fix minutes after you verified it live
- **source:** hit directly, webdesign_uk_build_service lane, 2026-08-11.
  `bugs_open`/HANDOFF for this incident:
  `webdesign_uk_build_service/NOTES_webdesign_uk_build_service.md`
  2026-08-11 entry
- **added:** 2026-08-11, webdesign_uk_build_service lane

### A correctly-filed `triaged` build item can sit for HOURS while the dispatcher visibly works — the fleet queue serves ONE site per tick, oldest item first

- **footprint:** `site_work_items` (any `pipeline='build'` filing); `scheduled_tasks` row `build-pipeline-trigger`; `agent_definitions` `type='build-pipeline-trigger'` step `find_dispatchable_site`; `platform/orchestration/actions/load_work_item_actions.go`
- **fires when:** you file a `triaged` item and expect the "picked up in minutes" that this estate's runbooks record (a real recreation ran ~5 min end to end on 08-10). The trigger fires every 120s but `find_dispatchable_site` selects **ONE site per tick, ordered by the fleet's globally OLDEST dispatchable item** (`ORDER BY wi.created_at ASC … LIMIT 1`) — so any site holding older triaged backlog outranks yours on every tick, indefinitely. Measured 2026-08-11 ~15:30Z: 7 sites held ~273 items older than a just-filed one, 81 of them 18 days old; the fresh item sat 80+ minutes with zero errors anywhere.
- **the tell: there is none in your item's row.** It stays `triaged`, `attempt_count` 0, no orchestration row — exactly what a dropped Kafka message, a dead queue, or a bad filing also look like. The reassuring-direction misread is "my filing is wrong, re-file" (a duplicate) or "the queue is dead, debug it" (it is fine); the fleet completing OTHER sites' items in the same minutes greps like health, and IS health — for them.
- **the check:** three reads separate starved from broken — (1) your row is dispatchable (`status/attempt_count/approval_mode/depends_on`), (2) the site is unlocked with no `claimed` item hogging its slot, (3) `scheduled_tasks.last_triggered_at` for `build-pipeline-trigger` is fresh. All three true = starved, not broken: your position is "behind every older item fleet-wide", queryable with one CTE (mortgagecalculator RUNBOOK §15). Do NOT re-file, and do not bump `priority` — site selection never reads it (the per-site pickup does, and there it is `priority ASC`: LOWER first).
- **why re-filing cannot help, mechanically** (added 2026-08-11 by the noted.co.uk lane, which hit this entry's exact case): selection reads `created_at`, and `refreshOpenWorkItemSQL()` (`load_work_item_actions.go:1417`) sets **`updated_at = NOW()` and never `created_at`** — so a re-file either no-ops against the open row or creates a newer row that sorts further back. The "Do NOT re-file" above is therefore not a caution, it is an impossibility.
- **do NOT measure the drain with the *eligible* count** — the selector excludes a site entirely while any of its items is `claimed`, so one claim drops that site's whole backlog out of the count and a release restores it. That figure read 564→501→419 in ten minutes and implied a 21-minute ETA against a true ~6h. The stable quantity is *pending items older than yours* (`status IN ('triaged','approved') AND created_at < <yours>`), which no claim can move; divide by the completion rate for equally-old items for an ETA.
- **second measurement, different lane and time** (2026-08-11 18:26Z, `noted.co.uk`, dispatched 17:00Z): **589 pending items older than it across 19 sites**, draining **~95/hour** (steady 13:00–17:00) ⇒ **~6h**, trigger firing every 2.5 min throughout. Corroborates the ~273/7-site reading above three hours later and shows the backlog is estate-scale, not a one-off. Mildly reassuring corollary: ordering is by `created_at`, so newly filed work sorts *behind* you and the set ahead is closed — unless an older `deferred`/`blocked`/`detected` item is moved to `triaged`.
- **the sanctioned bypass:** one `orchestrate` message pinning `build-dispatch-loop` to the site (precedent `scripts/initial_messages/180_adoption/081b_trigger_dispatch_gamesdesign.sh`; worked twice on 2026-08-11, claimed within a minute each time). Blast radius = that site's `triaged`/`approved` items only — enumerate them first. kcat exit 0 is not delivery; the only proof is the item flipping `claimed`.
- **source:** live `find_dispatchable_site` config + `load_work_item_actions.go:681`, queue measured 2026-08-11. Remedy + pre-checks: `mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption/RUNBOOK_mortgagecalculator_couk.md` §15
- **added:** 2026-08-11, mortgagecalculator.co.uk adoption lane

### `spec->>'audit_source'` names FIVE producers "design-audit" — the per-auditor label each agent sets in its config is silently dead

- **footprint:** `site_work_items` `spec->>'audit_source'` · `platform/orchestration/actions/write_audit_findings_action.go` (`DeployImageAsset`-family Defaults shadow: `Defaults{audit_source:"design-audit"}` + `inputs.Get("audit_source")` at `:495`) · the step configs of `brief-fidelity-auditor`, `content-quality-auditor`, `site-review-agent`, `visual-design-auditor` · any census, join or filter that attributes findings to a producer by `audit_source`
- **fires when:** you measure "which producers file this item_type" — exactly what `bugs_open/213`'s regression guard tells you to do via `spec->>'audit_source'` — or you filter one auditor's output for review. The four agents above each set a distinctive static (`'brief-fidelity-audit'`, `'content-quality-audit'`, `'site-review'`, `'visual-design-audit'`); every one is shadowed by the spec Default (`bugs_open/231`: against a defaulted field, only a resolving dotted path can win, and the action reads via the inputs path, unlike the ~20 sibling actions that read config directly). All their findings carry `design-audit`. The result LOOKS right: `design-audit` is a real, expected label, the count is plausible, and there is no row shape that says "mislabelled".
- **the check:** zero rows fleet-wide carry any of the four intended labels (`SELECT DISTINCT spec->>'audit_source' FROM site_work_items WHERE spec ? 'audit_source'` — three values as of 2026-08-11: `design-audit`, `tool-acceptance-tier4`, NULL). Proof row of the collapse: `item_type='audit_finding_brief_fidelity'` (2026-07-24) with `audit_source='design-audit'`. What still holds: `audit_source IS NOT NULL` as the audit-vs-discovery split. What does not: ANY per-auditor attribution, until the shadow is fixed (options costed in `bugs_open/231`, 2026-08-11 section). Detector: `scripts/audit-default-shadowed-keys.sh` fires on this and the whole class.

### The 090 diagnosis loop cannot read a Kubernetes env var — so any hypothesis whose decisive fact lives in a pod's ENVIRONMENT comes back with no verdict, and the verdict it *would* have reached is the reassuring one

- **footprint:** `090_TRIGGER_needs_diagnosis_v1.sh` · `diagnosis_artifacts` · `agent_definitions.env_vars` · any symptom naming `os.Getenv(...)`, `CHASSIS_DB_MAX_OPEN_CONNS`, `CHASSIS_INTAKE_MODE`, `IMAGE_BUCKET`, `DATABASE_URL` or any other environment-driven switch
- **fires when:** you file a 090 whose question is "is this override consequential?" / "is this feature actually enabled?" — i.e. anything that turns on whether an env var is SET. The loop's evidence surface is **the repo plus `clients_db`**. A deployment's env block is neither. It has no `kubectl`.
- **the tell: there is none in the run.** Measured 2026-08-11 (correlation `105970e4-dd02-4654-9536-84a2dd6a3da2`): the loop asked exactly the right question, went looking for the key in `agent_definitions.env_vars`, got **`(0 rows)`**, re-ran the identical query a second iteration under the F0.5 persistence rule and got `(0 rows)` again — **two checks blind the same way agreeing with each other** — then burned all 5 iterations and terminated `COMPLETED` with **five `bundle` artifacts, zero `council_report`, and no `doc_notes` verdict**. A completed run with no verdict looks exactly like a run that found nothing worth saying.
- **why it is dangerous rather than merely useless:** the evidence it *could* reach pointed the wrong way. `(0 rows)` for the key reads as "nothing sets this, so the override is a harmless no-op" — and the live answer was that **2 pods of 95 set it, both of them the pods the symptom was about**. Had the loop emitted a verdict on what it had, it would have been a confident REFUTED, and the filing session would have closed a real bug.
- **the check:** before filing, ask whether your decisive fact lives in the repo or in `clients_db`. If it lives in a pod's environment, **get it yourself first and put it in the symptom text as a stated fact**, so the loop is reasoning from it instead of hunting for it:
  ```bash
  kubectl -n ai-persona-system exec <pod> -- sh -c 'echo "[$YOUR_VAR]"'
  kubectl -n ai-persona-system get deploy <name> -o json | \
    python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print([(e['name'],e.get('value')) for c in d['spec']['template']['spec']['containers'] for e in c.get('env',[])])"
  ```
  And when a 090 returns `COMPLETED` with no `council_report` row, **read the last bundle's `data_requests` section before concluding anything** — it shows what the model went looking for and what it got back, which is where the blind spot is visible. `SELECT body FROM diagnosis_artifacts WHERE correlation_id='<run corr>' AND iteration=<max>`.
- **do not confuse with** the `UNVERIFIABLE` verdict (that one means the question was wrong). This is a run that reached **no verdict at all**, and the cause is the evidence surface, not the question.
- **source:** run `105970e4` filed and read 2026-08-11 by the bugfix 246 lane; the fact it could not see was `CHASSIS_DB_MAX_OPEN_CONNS=12` on both `agent-chassis` replicas. Full account: `docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_246_shared_pool_ownership/NOTES_shared_pool_ownership.md`
- **added:** 2026-08-11, bugfix 246 shared-pool-ownership lane

### Re-adopting a site silently drops the `structure` spec's opt-in flags — the pilot stops being a pilot and the fix reads as broken

- **footprint:** `site_specs` `aspect='structure'`, `apply_adoption_plan_action.go`,
  `WriteSiteSpecAction` / `siteSpecDeepMerge`, `siteUsesFlatURLs`,
  `siteIdentityPolicyFor`, `url_shape`, `honour_realised_identity`,
  `twin_identity_snap`, `stem_twin_snap`
- **fires when:** you enable a per-site behaviour flag in the structure spec — the
  URL shape (BLD-018) or any of the three page-identity gates (PLAN-048) — and
  the site is later re-adopted, or you are debugging why an enabled flag appears
  to do nothing
- **the tell: none, and the failure imitates the thing you would test next.** The
  flags read `false`, which is the default and today's behaviour, so the pipeline
  runs normally and the pages come out exactly as they did before the fix existed.
  The natural conclusion is "the fix does not work" or "the flag never took", and
  both send you into the Go code rather than at the spec row
- **why it happens:** the ordinary writer is safe — `WriteSiteSpecAction`
  DEEP-MERGES a partial update over the current spec, so unknown keys survive.
  `apply_adoption_plan_action.go` does not: it supersedes the current row and
  INSERTs freshly-marshalled JSON, so every key it does not itself write is gone.
- **the check:** ask the row, not the code, and ask it *after* any adoption run:
  ```sql
  SELECT data ? 'url_shape'              AS has_url_shape,
         data ? 'honour_realised_identity' AS has_honour,
         data ? 'twin_identity_snap'     AS has_twin,
         data ? 'stem_twin_snap'         AS has_stem,
         updated_at
  FROM site_specs WHERE site_id = $1 AND aspect = 'structure' AND is_current;
  ```
  A `false` here means ABSENT, which is not the same as "set to off" — use `?`
  (key presence), never `->>'k' = 'true'`, or the two states look identical.
- **it fails SAFE, which is why it survives unnoticed:** a dropped key can only
  ever read as `false`, so nothing turns ON by itself and no live page moves. The
  cost is silent loss of an intended pilot, not damage
- **distinct from the neighbouring `pinned` entry:** that one is about the `pinned`
  COLUMN being dropped by `write_site_spec`; this is about `data` KEYS being
  dropped by adoption. Same table, different mechanism, and `pinned` would not
  have protected these flags even if it worked
- **source:** raised by the council gate's `guardian` seat, round 2 of
  `bugs_open/215`'s quiet-mode submission (corr `56e13695`), 2026-08-11; verified
  by reading both write paths
- **FIX COMMITTED 2026-08-11 (`19acfc895`, 241 lane) — ~~INERT UNTIL THE NEXT ROLL~~
  LIVE since `v1.0.1294` (2026-08-13, artefact-verified: revision label ancestry +
  literal `carryForwardStructureSpecKeys` in `/proc/1/exe` with near-miss control 0;
  re-verified on `v1.0.1295`).** `carryForwardStructureSpecKeys` in
  `apply_adoption_plan_action.go` merges the current structure row's unknown keys
  under adoption's fresh write (all unknown keys, fresh wins; fails open). The check
  above remains worth running after an adoption only if the pod predates 1294.
  Do not re-fix; council trail corr `70256656` (APPROVED).
- > **NOW LIVE — verified 2026-08-12 ~13:00Z, chassis `v1.0.1290`.** The roll the
  > line above was waiting for has happened. `carryForwardStructureSpecKeys` →
  > **PRESENT on both replicas** (`8tjhm`, `vj2rt`), one-letter near-miss
  > `carryForwardStructureSpecKeyz` → **absent on both**, and `19acfc895` is an
  > ancestor of HEAD. **So the adoption path no longer drops the keys.** Keep the
  > check anyway — it is still the right instrument for "did my flag take?", and it
  > is the only thing that distinguishes ABSENT from set-to-off. Corrected by the
  > 215 quiet-mode lane, which needed the answer to read its own gates and found
  > the status one roll stale.
- **added:** 2026-08-11, bugs_open/215 quiet-mode lane

### The page-identity dark-launch counter is NOT a passive instrument — an `*_OBSERVED` row is a duplicate that WAS allowed through, and the count conflates two opposite events

- **footprint:** `PLAN_PAGE_IDENTITY_TWIN_OBSERVED`, `PLAN_PAGE_STEM_TWIN_OBSERVED`,
  `PLAN_PAGE_STEM_TWIN_REFUSED`, `PLAN_PAGE_IDENTITY_SNAPPED`, `agent_error_log`,
  `observeOrSnap`, `eligible`, `recordIdentitySnaps`, `reconcilePlanWithRealised`,
  `twin_identity_snap`, `stem_twin_snap`
- **fires when:** you read the PLAN-048 dark-launch counters to decide whether to
  enable a page-identity gate — the ordering `bugs_open/215`'s own handoff
  prescribes — or you quote an `*_OBSERVED` count as a rate of anything
- **the tell: none. The counter reads exactly like a camera and behaves like a
  turnstile.** Nothing in the name, the severity or the row's shape says the
  observation had a cost, and the natural reading of "observed" is "watched
  without touching"
- **why it happens:** with the gate off, `observeOrSnap`
  (`v3_site_actions.go:5852-5868`) records the finding and **returns without
  snapping**, so the plan keeps both identities and the name-keyed upsert proceeds.
  The remedy string it writes says so outright — *"each of these is a second page
  identity about to be written"* — but you only see that if you read a row, not a
  `count(*)`
- **the second half, which is the part that will actually mislead you:** an
  `*_OBSERVED` row means one of **two opposite things**, and the counter cannot tell
  them apart. If the plan entry's twin is **already realised**, it is pure
  detection of damage you already have and nothing new is written. If it is **not**,
  a fresh duplicate page row was just minted. Same code, same counter, same
  severity
- **the check:** never read the counter alone — join each row's `plan_name` context
  back against `pages` and classify before quoting a total:
  ```sql
  SELECT e.error_code,
         e.context->>'plan_name'     AS plan_name,
         e.context->>'realised_name' AS realised_name,
         EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pages p
                WHERE p.name = e.context->>'plan_name'
                  AND p.status NOT IN ('deleted','archived')) AS plan_name_already_realised
  FROM agent_error_log e
  WHERE e.error_code IN ('PLAN_PAGE_IDENTITY_TWIN_OBSERVED','PLAN_PAGE_STEM_TWIN_OBSERVED')
  ORDER BY e.occurred_at DESC;
  ```
  `plan_name_already_realised = true` ⇒ harmless re-detection. `false` ⇒ that row
  **is** a new duplicate. And before reading any zero as evidence, confirm demand
  existed: a plan whose `pages` rows were created *after* the plan row is a FIRST
  build, which cannot exercise the reconciler at all
- **`*_REFUSED` is the safe one, and its silence is engineered:** where the plan
  already carries both spellings, `eligible` (`:5834-5846`) returns false and the
  path_key and canonical layers skip **recording nothing at all** — only the stem
  layer logs a refusal. So a site whose duplicates are both in-plan
  (robot-hands.com, all three pairs) is **invisible to the OBSERVED counters by
  design**, and its zero says nothing about its duplicates
- **consequence for the enable decision:** "read the population, then enable" is
  only free where the duplicates already exist. Enabling on a site whose pairs are
  both already realised (fundamentallyai.com) harvests the same evidence at zero
  new damage; waiting for a counter to fill on a site whose next duplicate is
  *new* buys the evidence with the defect
- **kin to "Observe-only is not a property your discovery check can HAVE"** (2026-08-11,
  vigilant_designer_offer_analysis lane, elsewhere in this file). **Same shape, third
  subsystem, found independently** — there it was a discovery check whose "just
  looking" pass promoted work items; here it is a reconciler layer whose "just
  counting" pass lets a duplicate through. Neither lane knew of the other. **Treat
  "this only observes" as a claim to verify in the off-path, not a property a
  mechanism can be described as having** — on current evidence this estate does not
  reliably build passive observers, and the two entries together are worth more than
  either alone
- **source:** 2026-08-12, `bugs_open/215` quiet-mode lane, reading the counters for
  the first time after the `v1.0.1290` roll. I first concluded the dark launch was
  *inherently* self-harming and was wrong — the `eligible` arm is what
  distinguishes the harmless case, and it had to be opened rather than inferred
  from the counter's name. Full trace: `brochure_component_library/NOTES_*.md`
  2026-08-12, and the per-pair prediction table in the `bugs_open/215` file
- **added:** 2026-08-12, bugs_open/215 quiet-mode lane

### A `page_components` scan has NO site of its own — an asset-path query sweeps the whole fleet, and `/assets/images/<prefix>-` is a namespace every site shares

- **footprint:** `page_components`, `model_lifecycle.artefacts`, any "which pages
  reference asset X" query
- **the trap:** `page_components` reaches a site only through `pages.site_id`, so
  a query that joins `pages` but forgets the filter returns **other sites' rows,
  silently and correctly**. It compounds with the second half: every site on the
  platform serves its images from the same `/assets/images/` path shape, so
  `LIKE '/assets/images/case-study-%'` matches another site's completely unrelated
  files. The result is a real row, a real page, a real slot name — nothing looks
  wrong
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** you then confirm it
  by curling the path against the domain you are working on, and it **404s** —
  which reads as "this page of mine is broken" when it actually means "this is not
  my page". The confirmation cannot fail, because a foreign page's URL always
  404s on your domain. Two checks, blind the same way, agreeing with each other
- **the check:** put the site in the query and the DOMAIN in the output, so a
  foreign row is visible as foreign —
  `SELECT s.domain, p.url … FROM page_components pc JOIN pages p ON p.id=pc.page_id JOIN sites s ON s.id=p.site_id`
  — and compare **filenames, not prefixes**:
  `SELECT DISTINCT regexp_matches(pc.content_data::text, '/assets/images/(case-study-[a-z0-9-]+\.[a-z]+)', 'g')`.
  Different slugs or a different extension coming back is the tell
- **and read `content_data::text`, not `jsonb_each_text`, for this question:** the
  flat form sees only top-level values, so a nested `{"image":{"url":…}}` never
  matches an anchored prefix and the count comes back plausibly small rather than
  wrong-looking. Size the positive control before trusting it — mine returned
  **1**, which passes a "is it non-zero" test while discriminating nothing
- **source:** `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-11 (finetuning lane) — a page belonging to
  `ai-agent-orchestration.com` was recorded in a handoff as finetuning.uk's "only
  current reference in the whole site", and became a standing next-action for the
  following thread. Its five files were `.png` with slugs this site has never used
- **added:** 2026-08-11, finetuning service lane

### `improvement-sweep`'s eligibility guard counts `triaged` AND `detected` — so the sweep re-locks sites with its OWN promotions, and a falling `detected` reads as progress while open work grows

- **footprint:** `scheduled_tasks.pre_query`, `improvement-sweep`,
  `site_work_items.status`, `triage_detect_items_action.go`, `item_type='page_rerender'`

- **the trap:** the `pre_query` skips any site with **≥50** rows in
  `status IN ('triaged','detected') AND pipeline='build'`. Promotion moves a row from one
  member of that list to the other and **does not reduce the count**. So the sweep's own
  output counts against its own eligibility: it fires, promotes, and pushes the site back
  over the guard. Clearing a site *into* eligibility buys one or two fires, not a state
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** the number everyone watches is
  `detected`, and it **falls convincingly** — ours went 193 → 25 in five hours, which is
  exactly what a drain looks like. Meanwhile `triaged` rose from ~0 to 381, open work
  (`detected+triaged+unresolved`) went ~273 → 544, and sites over the guard went **5 → 1
  (after a deliberate 226-row park) → 8**, i.e. *worse than the state the park was performed
  to fix*. Every individual figure is real; the reassuring one is the one that is quoted
- **the second half, which is what makes it expensive:** the sweep is a **producer**, not
  just a promoter. Its first step is `call_quality_discovery` — a full LLM site pass that
  **files new work items** — so it adds arrivals (~105/h measured) to a path that clears at
  ~50/h. Cadence does not fix a divergence of that shape; a slower cadence only slows the
  divergence
- **the check, before you enable it or judge it:** never grade this from `detected`. Take
  the guard's own census, before and after —
  `SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE b<50) eligible, count(*) FILTER (WHERE b>=50) locked FROM
   (SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM site_work_items wi WHERE wi.site_id=s.id AND wi.status IN
   ('triaged','detected') AND wi.pipeline='build') b FROM sites s WHERE s.status IN
   ('active','deployed')) t;`
  — and put **arrivals against completions** side by side (`count(*)` by `date_trunc('hour',
  created_at)` vs by `updated_at` filtered to `status='complete'`). If arrivals exceed
  completions the queue is moving, not draining, however good `detected` looks
- **and do not assume stopping it stops the drain:** it does not. The re-render execution is
  a **separate always-on path at ~50/h**, proven by hours when the sweep was disabled
  (08-11 10:00/11:00 = 49/48; 08-10 13:00–15:00 = 85/110/41). A handoff in this estate
  asserted the opposite for a day — see `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-11 (bugfix 122 lane)
- **source:** bugfix 122 lane, `NOTES_contrast_ink_slots.md` 2026-08-11 evening entry;
  migration `389` parked 226 `contrast_failure` rows to buy the eligibility this then spent
- **added:** 2026-08-11, bugfix 122 lane

### `git commit … | tail -N` throws away every pre-commit advisory — the scope report, all 17 pattern checks, and the architecture signal
- **footprint:** `git commit`, `.githooks/pre-commit`, `scripts/commit-scope-report.sh`,
  `scripts/pattern-check.py`, `scripts/commit-advisory-postuse.py`, `.claude/settings.json`

- **the trap:** the pre-commit hook prints **first**; git prints its `[branch sha] subject`
  and `N files changed` summary **last**. So `git commit <paths> -m "…" 2>&1 | tail -5` —
  the near-universal house form — keeps exactly what you asked for and silently discards
  the commit-scope report (the estate's main defence against committing another session's
  work), every `pattern-check.py` finding, and the architecture RFC-trigger signal
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** the **commit-msg** hook's
  output prints later and therefore survives, so the council-trailer nudge arrives on cue
  and the hook machinery reads as alive and quiet. "No warnings" and "warnings cut off
  above the window" are indistinguishable at the tool result
- **it is not rare and it is not one lane:** measured 2026-08-11 over every commit made
  through the tool since the report shipped — **1,199 of 2,669 multi-file commits (45%)
  never delivered the block; 1,137 of those misses (95%) were the `| tail`; 258 distinct
  sessions**. Misses cluster at `tail -N` ≤ 8 (median 5); commits that delivered despite a
  pipe cluster at N > 8. `scripts/advisory-delivery-sweep.py`
- **the check:** you no longer have to remember — **OPP-007**
  (`scripts/commit-advisory-postuse.py`, a `PostToolUse` hook wired in
  `.claude/settings.json`) re-runs both scripts against the new sha and delivers the result
  out of band, where no pipe of yours can reach it. If you have disabled hooks or are
  outside this repo, read it back yourself:
  `scripts/commit-scope-report.sh --commit <sha>; scripts/pattern-check.py --commit <sha>`.
  Widening the pipe works too (`| tail -30`), but do not rely on remembering it
- **do NOT "fix" this by moving the advisory to a `post-commit` hook** — verified in a
  scratch repo: `post-commit` output also lands *before* git's summary, so the same
  `tail -3` eats it. Leaving the command's stdout altogether is the only escape
- **the general shape, worth more than this instance:** a check is only as good as its
  delivery, and delivery is a property of *how the caller invokes the command*, not of the
  check. Measure at the reader, never at the detector. The sibling trap one layer over: a
  `PostToolUse` hook that writes to **stderr** and exits 0 reaches nobody while looking
  armed (`scripts/memory-index.py`, mute for six days)
- **source:** `docs026_concept_register/FINDINGS_2026-08-11_advisory_delivery.md`; register
  OPP-007; the motivating case is OPP-006's first live miss (`5c7b115c5`, `tail -8`,
  recorded stdout exactly 8 lines)
- **added:** 2026-08-11, concept-register lane

### A CSS custom property "default" written as a self-reference — `--x: var(--x, #good)` — is a cycle: the fallback can NEVER apply, and the subtree is poisoned even where `:root` defines the token

- **footprint:** any authored or generated component CSS; `page_components.rendered_html` on tool pages; the tool-recreation/tool-generator output idiom (`agent_definitions` `type='tool-recreation-handler'`); migration `393_fix_self_referential_css_vars_three_tool_components.sql`
- **fires when:** you write, generate, or review a theme bridge like `.tool-page { --primary-color: var(--primary-color, #0b2545); }` intending "site theme if defined, else my default". Per css-variables-1 §3 a custom property referencing itself is a dependency cycle (self-loop) → **invalid at computed-value time**; the fallback is part of the cycle and cannot rescue it, and an ancestor's definition is NOT consulted. Every `var(--x)` in the subtree without its own fallback then collapses to the property's initial value.
- **the tell: none in the source, and the source is actively reassuring** — the line *displays* both the override intent and a sensible default, so review reads it as belt-and-braces. It passed this estate's review twice (2026-08-08 and 2026-08-11, same generator, different pages). Measured 2026-08-11 on mortgagecalculator.co.uk: `:root` defined `--primary-color: #b59230`, yet `.tool-page` computed **empty**; primary buttons rendered transparent with a white label = **1.05:1** on three pages, while a sibling page using a plain literal measured 15.54:1. The page otherwise works — layout survives because transparent falls through to chrome backgrounds — so nothing else fails loudly.
- **the check, mechanical:** grep the CSS for `(--[A-Za-z-]+): *var\( *\1[,)]` — any hit is a bug, no valid use exists. For ground truth on a live page ask the browser, never the source: `getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue('--x')` returning `''` while `:root` shows a value IS this trap (probe recipe: mortgagecalculator NOTES 2026-08-11 afternoon). The correct patterns are a plain literal, or a two-name bridge (`--primary-color: var(--color-cta-bg, #0b2545)`).
- **kin, not duplicate:** `a-css-fallback-is-present-and-inoperative` (memory) is the general "fallback in source ≠ fallback applied"; this entry is the specific idiom that GUARANTEES it, plus the subtree poisoning that defeats the ":root defines it, so we're fine" rebuttal.
- **source:** migration 393 (+ header analysis); `mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption/NOTES` 2026-08-11; found by the tool-acceptance vision pass's first run (`vision_finding` 15:35:58Z), fixed same day at owner direction
- **added:** 2026-08-11, mortgagecalculator.co.uk adoption lane

### `status='deferred'` on `site_work_items` does NOT mean undispatchable — only the PAIR (`deferred` + empty `handler_agent`) does, and 95% of deferred rows are not that pair

- **footprint:** `site_work_items.status`; `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/remit.go` (the "double lock"); `platform/orchestration/actions/triage_detect_items_action.go`; `diagnose_triage_action.go` (the capability-gap roadmap query); any new writer choosing a status so its row "cannot be picked up"
- **fires when:** you file a row you intend nobody to claim, and you reach for `deferred` because `capability_gap` uses it — or, in the other direction, you read a `deferred` row and conclude nothing will act on it. [MEASURED 2026-08-11] `deferred` carries **316 rows across 14 item_types** (`add_tool`, `contrast_failure`, `needs_page`, `page_rerender`, `undeployed_asset`, …); **only 15** also carry an empty `handler_agent`. So the status alone is an ordinary parked state that a handler is named for, and the *undispatchability* comes from the empty handler, not from the word.
- **the tell: none — both readings are self-consistent.** `remit.go` calls it a "double lock" and the phrase reads as belt-and-braces on ONE mechanism; the estate's own register entry for `capability_gap` describes the pair, so quoting it while implementing only half looks like compliance. Nothing errors either way: a `deferred` row with a handler simply waits, and a reader who assumed inertness is wrong silently.
- **the check:** `SELECT status, count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE handler_agent='') AS empty_handler FROM site_work_items GROUP BY 1;` — read BOTH columns. And check the consumer side rather than assuming: the dispatch loop selects `status IN ('triaged','approved')`, the promoter selects `status='detected'`, and `diagnose_triage`'s roadmap view selects `item_type='capability_gap' OR status='deferred'` — so a `deferred` row IS surfaced somewhere, which is usually what you want and is not the same as being claimed.
- **kin:** WII-008's `needs_human_review` note (a non-terminal dedup slot with no handler is a DECISION queue, not a work queue) — same shape, different status; the dedup index's terminal-status list, which contains neither status, so both hold their slot.
- **source:** council round 1 on corr `fc082c4a-4b00-4835-8ffe-11a55e53f47a` (`guardian [medium]`: *"No existing 'deferred' status is confirmed live on this table … a new status value can leak into a queue it was never meant to enter"*) — the objection asked for the check, and the check found the finer fact; WII-015, `bugs_open/213` D3
- **added:** 2026-08-11, bugfix_213 lane

### `grep -Lq PATTERN` prints the files that DO match — `-q` wins over `-L`, silently, and the answer you get is the exact complement of the one you asked for

- **footprint:** any shell survey of the shape `for f in …; do grep -Lq PAT "$f" && echo "$f"; done`; census scripts under `scripts/`; ad-hoc "which files DON'T do X" greps
- **fires when:** you enumerate the files *lacking* something — "which checks are not site-scoped", "which actions never call the helper" — and combine `-L` (files without a match) with `-q` (quiet, exit 0 on match) so the exit status you branch on is `-q`'s. Every line printed is a file that DOES contain the pattern. No error, no warning, and the output is a plausible-looking list of the right size.
- **the tell: only plausibility.** The inverted list looks like a real finding — mine said 20 of ~50 discovery checks ignore `SiteID`, which would have been a substantial architectural fact, and it was 100% wrong (the true answer is one file, and it is a helpers file with no check in it).
- **the check:** use `grep -rLE PAT <files>` with no `-q` and READ the list, then spot-check one named file by opening it. A one-file confirmation costs seconds and inverts the whole conclusion when it is wrong. More generally: a negative-space survey is a claim about ABSENCE, so verify one member of the answer set before quoting the count.
- **kin:** the estate's other silent-shell traps (`kcat -P` publishing nothing at exit 0; `grep` returning 0 matches and no error on ISO-8859 input) — same family: the shell answers a different question and reports success.
- **source:** `bugfix_213_verifier_producer_join/NOTES` 2026-08-11 evening (caught before it reached a council reply, by implausibility rather than by process)

### `grep -aq <ancestor-commit-sha> /proc/1/exe` reads absent even when that commit genuinely shipped — the binary embeds only the ONE commit it was built FROM, never its ancestors

- **footprint:** any provenance check on a Go backend binary; `agent-chassis`/any service using the `ldflags`-injected `git_commit` build stamp (BLD-019); `bugfix_153_build_provenance/RUNBOOK` R9c
- **fires when:** you want to know "did commit X ship" and, instead of asking the binary what it WAS BUILT FROM and then checking ancestry with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, you grep the running binary directly for commit X's own hex string. The build stamp is a single string constant (the exact commit HEAD was pinned to at build time), not a manifest of history — so grepping for any OTHER commit's hash, however genuinely merged into that history, finds nothing.
- **the tell: a clean negative control makes the absence look trustworthy.** `grep -aqc "<mine>" /proc/1/exe` → absent, and a fresh random-hex string on the same pod → also absent — the probe LOOKS well-controlled (both a real check and a negative control agree), because the control only proves the grep mechanism works, not that the QUESTION being asked was the right one. I ran exactly this, on two commits, on two replicas, all four came back "absent", and concluded a fleet release that had actually already shipped both commits had not.
- **the check:** get the binary's OWN stamp first — the "build provenance" log line (per-service, tail may scroll on a busy service; if so use the build-window method in `bugfix_153_build_provenance/RUNBOOK` §R9b(ii)/R9c instead of guessing) — then `git merge-base --is-ancestor <your-commit> <the stamp>`. Only grep the binary directly for a literal that is genuinely NEW source text (a log message, an error string) you added in that exact commit, never for a commit hash that isn't the build's own.
- **kin:** the fleet's other "clean control, wrong question" traps (a `[MEASURED]` figure that could not have come out otherwise; a filtered count shipped inside a denominator) — the control was procedurally fine and the premise underneath it was not.
- **source:** `staged_component_build` lane, 2026-08-11, resuming from a handoff mid-council-review; caught before being asserted anywhere durable, by cross-checking against `bugfix_153_build_provenance`'s own documented method rather than trusting the four-way "absent" result.
- **added:** 2026-08-11, staged_component_build lane
- **added:** 2026-08-11, bugfix_213 lane

### "Observe-only" is not a property your discovery check can HAVE — the improvement loop promotes EVERY `detected` row on a site it reaches, with no type filter

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/triage_detect_items_action.go` (`TriageDetectedItemsAction`), `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/` (any new check), `site_work_items.status`, `improvement-loop`'s `triage_findings` step
- **fires when:** you ship a new discovery check "observe-only first" — the standard, sanctioned way to land one (IMP-016) — and describe its findings as inspectable-before-acting because you file them at `detected` and route nothing. That is true only until the improvement loop next sweeps one of the affected sites. Its promoter is `UPDATE site_work_items SET status='triaged', pipeline=$2 WHERE site_id = $1 AND status = 'detected'` — **no type filter, no ownership filter, no cap** (the action's own header says so, and its `SingleOwner: true` is about there being exactly one such promoter, not about which rows it takes). Your rows are promoted with everyone else's, then claimed by whatever `handler_agent` you named.
- **the tell, and it is that there ISN'T one:** nothing warns you, and the sites you hand-tested are usually the ones the loop has not reached, so the observe-only reading survives every check you make. Ours held for two days and 21 sites, and read as true in four documents, because the loop simply had not got to those sites yet.
- **the consequences worth knowing BEFORE you file, not after:** (1) **a finding cannot be parked** — demoting `triaged` → `detected` guarantees re-promotion, since that is exactly the predicate it selects on, and `cancelled`/`wont_fix` are terminal so `idx_swi_dedup` releases the slot and your detector re-files on its next rotation; ~~there is no third state~~ **CORRECTED 2026-08-12 (mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption lane): there IS a third state — `deferred`, which is selected by neither the promoter nor dispatch, and is absent from `idx_swi_dedup`'s exclusion list so it also blocks the re-file. It parks a finding permanently, which is what this entry wanted; it is a TRAP rather than a remedy, because the parked finding can never be re-raised either. See the `deferred` entry at the end of this file.** (2) **your `handler_agent` will actually be called**, so it must be able to READ your spec (see the sibling entry / `bugs_open/255`, where it could not and refused as "there is no gap"). (3) design the check to be RIGHT, not to be reviewed first.
- **the check:** before calling a new check observe-only, ask whether the loop has swept the sites you are quoting — `SELECT status, count(*), min(created_at) FROM site_work_items WHERE site_id = '<a site with your findings>' GROUP BY 1;`. If anything on that site is `triaged`, the loop reaches it and your findings are dispatchable. To bound it the other way: a site whose `detected` rows are days old has NOT been swept in days, so "wait for the loop" is not a bounded wait either — hand-fire when timing matters.
- **kin:** `a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact` one level up — both are about reasoning over what YOUR code does while the estate does something else with its output.
- **source:** `vigilant_designer_offer_analysis` lane, 2026-08-11: B3's four findings, described as observe-only since 08-09, were promoted by the loop within one afternoon; one reached its handler and exposed `bugs_open/255`.
- **added:** 2026-08-11, vigilant_designer_offer_analysis lane

### A `handler_agent` named in a routing decision is an UNCHECKED CONTRACT — nothing verifies your item's spec carries the keys that handler reads

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/` (any check setting `HandlerAgent`), `site_work_items.spec`, `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/remit.go` (`HandlerStepConfig`), `platform/orchestration/actions/apply_gap_plan_action.go` (`applyNotActionable`)
- **fires when:** you route a new item type at an existing agent because its job description fits — "a missing conversion path is a content gap, so: `content-gap-planner`". The routing is correct in intent and the handler is live and registered, so every check you can think of passes: the agent exists, the item is claimable, the dispatch works. What nothing checks is whether your `spec` carries the fields that agent's prompt actually READS.
- **the tell is a refusal that reads as disagreement:** the handler comes back *not actionable* — "the content gap description and original category are both blank; there is no gap to evaluate" — which scans as **"your finding was wrong"** rather than "I could not read it". If the finding was hand-verified you will disbelieve the handler rather than suspect the shape, which is the wrong way round.
- **and the refusal is TERMINAL, so it repeats for ever:** `applyNotActionable` sets `wont_fix`; `wont_fix` is in `workItemTerminalStatuses` and is excluded by `idx_swi_dedup`'s own `WHERE` (read it from `pg_indexes`, not from the Go list), so the dedup slot is released and your detector re-files next rotation. One LLM call per rotation, indefinitely, with **nothing reading as broken** — no `failed`, no `unresolved`, no two-strike label, because `wont_fix` is a settled conclusion to every status query.
- **the check, and the seam already exists:** call `HandlerStepConfig(ctx, db, agentType, action)` and read the handler's **LIVE** step config before you file — its own doc comment explains why the Go source will not do (nav-link-fixer's live row carried three patterns where the Go default had four). Cheapest manual version: `SELECT jsonb_pretty(default_config->'workflow'->'steps') FROM agent_definitions WHERE type='<your handler>' AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL;` and grep the prompt for the spec keys it interpolates.
- **distinct from `bugs_closed/077`**, which is the same family one step LATER: there the handler runs and its transform provably cannot touch part of the population (remedy: split the population, file residue as `capability_gap`). Here the handler never gets as far as having a remit, because the item is unreadable — a remit split cannot fix it and a `capability_gap` would misdescribe it.
- **source:** `bugs_open/255` + `016b` §9, filed 2026-08-11 by the lane that caused it; diagnosis loop CONFIRMED first iteration (`64e5ab04`).
- **added:** 2026-08-11, vigilant_designer_offer_analysis lane

### `deferred` IS the third state the entry above says does not exist — a parked work item is undispatchable AND still holds its dedup slot, so it never runs and can never be re-filed

- **footprint:** `site_work_items.status`, `idx_swi_dedup`, `platform/orchestration/actions/claim_work_item_action.go` (`status IN ('triaged','approved')`), `platform/orchestration/actions/triage_detect_items_action.go`, `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/remit.go`
- **fires when:** you audit a site's queue to answer "is this being handled?" and read the rows as work in progress. A `deferred` row looks **more** live than a `detected` one, not less: it carries a real `handler_agent`, a real `priority` (ours were **98**, near the top), a real `item_key`, and no `error`. Every field says "queued". `attempt_count = 0` is the only hint, and it reads as "not started yet" rather than "will never start".
- **why it is a black hole, in three predicates that nobody reads together:** (1) dispatch claims `status IN ('triaged','approved')` — `deferred` is not selectable; (2) the promoter (`TriageDetectedItemsAction`) selects `status='detected'` — a `deferred` row is never promoted, by anything; (3) `deferred` is **absent from `idx_swi_dedup`'s exclusion list** (read it from `pg_indexes`: `status <> ALL (complete, verified, rejected, wont_fix, failed, unresolved, cancelled)`), so the row still occupies the `(site_id, item_key)` slot and the detector that found the problem **cannot re-file it**. Undispatchable and un-refilable at the same time.
- **the tell: age with a zero attempt count.** Ours sat **10 days** at priority 98 with `attempt_count = 0` and `handled_by` NULL, while the site was rebuilt, re-rendered and audited around them. Nothing ever reported them, because no status query treats `deferred` as a problem.
- **the check:** when you ask whether a finding is being handled, filter on what dispatch can actually see, not on the row's plausibility — `SELECT status, count(*), min(created_at), max(attempt_count) FROM site_work_items WHERE site_id='<sid>' GROUP BY 1;` and treat anything outside `('triaged','approved','claimed')` as **not going to happen without a hand-promotion**. To un-park: `UPDATE … SET status='triaged'` (there is no action that will do it for you).
- **CORRECTS the sibling entry above** ("Observe-only is not a property your discovery check can HAVE", 2026-08-11, vigilant_designer_offer_analysis): its consequence (1) states *"there is no third state"* between re-promotion and terminal-plus-refile. **There is, and this is it** — `deferred` parks a finding permanently, which is what that entry wanted and could not find. **Cost of the gap:** the reading held because nobody had looked for a status that is neither promoted nor terminal; four bulk-deferral batches on one site (07-31, 08-02, 08-03, 08-05) were invisible to every audit run over them. It is a *dangerous* parking spot rather than a useful one — a parked finding is also an unre-filable one — so the correction narrows the claim rather than reversing its advice.
- **source:** `mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption` lane, 2026-08-12, tracing why homepage cards had no imagery: the four `needs_imagery:section:index:1:icon_*` items were filed correctly on 08-02 and deferred 72 seconds later. Handoff §11.3. **[UNVERIFIED]** what performed the bulk deferral — no Go path writes `deferred` for these item types.
- **added:** 2026-08-12, mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption lane

### Chrome nav repair is ONE-DIRECTIONAL — a stored nav thins when a target stops being fetchable and never thickens when one starts, so a correct nav table can serve a one-item menu indefinitely

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/chrome_link_policy.go` (`markStaleChromeLinkSlot`, `LoadChromeLinkPolicy`), `platform/orchestration/actions/component_library.go` (`InjectHeader`, `InjectFooter`), `platform/orchestration/actions/render_site_components_action.go:656` (the idempotence EXISTS probe), `site_components.rendered_html`, `site_nav_items`
- **fires when:** a site serves a header with fewer nav links than `site_nav_items` holds, and you go looking for the missing rows. **The rows are there.** Chrome is written **once** behind the idempotence gate, so the stored header is a snapshot of which target pages were fetchable *at the moment it last rendered* — and the only repair channel, `markStaleChromeLinkSlot`, marks a slot when stored chrome contains an href the policy now **REFUSES**. A nav that is missing an item contains no offending href, so **nothing ever marks it stale**. Links can only leave.
- **the tell, and it is a trap in itself: "Home" always survives.** `loadFetchablePageSet` unconditionally injects `/` and `/index.html`, so the degenerate case renders as a plausible one-item menu rather than an empty bar or an error. `chrome_link_policy.go:70-77` says so in as many words — the state "nothing is deployed" *cannot* be detected from the surviving-item count.
- **the discriminator, when you have one page to look at:** compare the **footer** with the **header** on the same served page. The footer requests `primary+utility+legal` and the header requests `primary` alone, so a site whose data is fine but whose header froze shows the asymmetry immediately (ours: **16 footer links, 1 header link**). If both are thin, suspect the data; if only the header is, suspect the freeze.
- **the check:** never conclude from the served HTML. Read the stored artefact and the tables side by side — `SELECT slot_name, updated_at, (SELECT count(*) FROM regexp_matches(rendered_html,'<li><a href="([^"]*)"','g')) FROM site_components WHERE site_id='<sid>';` against `SELECT g.group_key, count(*) FROM site_nav_items i JOIN site_nav_groups g ON g.id=i.group_id WHERE i.site_id='<sid>' GROUP BY 1;` — **and compare `site_components.updated_at` against `pages.deployed_at`**: a page that deployed after the chrome was written is invisible to it for ever. Ours missed by 92 minutes (chrome 18:06Z, `/about/` 19:38Z).
- **not a bug in `ChromeLinkPolicy`:** dropping a never-deployed target is correct — it prevents a site-wide 404. The gap is that nothing re-renders when the target *arrives*. `chrome_link_policy.go:15-18` documents the mirror case (a dead CTA beside a filtered nav, `bugs_open/191`) on this same site; the omission direction has no channel at all.
- **kin:** `a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact`; and the general shape "a renderer fix is inert until something re-renders" (`016b` §9), which `191` answered for one direction only.
- **source:** `mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption` lane, 2026-08-12, owner reported "the top nav says just Home". Handoff §11.2. **Not yet through `090`** — treat the mechanism as one session's first-hand reading.
- **added:** 2026-08-12, mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption lane

### An unresolved dotted-path INPUT becomes a real filename — the asset deploys, git commits it, every step reports success, and the page 404s

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/deploy_image_asset_action.go`, `platform/storage/url_helpers.go` (`DeployedAssetPath`, `AssetKeyFilename`), `agent_definitions` step `input_mapping` for `asset-deployer` / `image-build-handler`, `site_work_items` rows of type `needs_hero_image` / `needs_imagery`
- **fires when:** a hero or imagery work item closes **`complete`** and the image is still missing from the page. You will check the obvious things — was it generated? stored? committed? — and every one of them says yes, because they all did happen. What went wrong is **where**: an `input_mapping` value like `input_data.asset_key` that does not resolve is passed through as a **literal string**, and `DeployedAssetPath` faithfully slugifies it into a filename. Ours shipped the hero to `/assets/images/input-data.asset-key.jpg`.
- **the tell is inside the work item's own `result`**, holding both paths at once: `"hero_url": "/assets/images/hero.jpg"` next to `"file_path": "/assets/images/input-data.asset-key.jpg"`. Nothing compares them. A filename containing a `.` in the stem, or hyphens where a config key had underscores, is the signature of a template that never resolved.
- **the check, and run BOTH URLs in one breath:** `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{size_download} %{content_type}\n'` against the path the page references **and** the path the deploy recorded. A 404 on the referenced path alone means "no hero"; a 404 there plus a **200 with real bytes** at the recorded path means "the hero exists and the path is wrong" — a different defect with a different fix, and you cannot tell them apart without the second call. (`DeployedAssetPath` returns the correct base name only when `assetKey == "" || assetKey == purpose`; an empty value is SAFE and a stale literal is not, which is why the optional-input marker `asset_key?` matters.)
- **why the guard you will find does not cover this:** the explicit `deploy_path` override was removed and is now actively refused (`bugs_open/179` finding A), with an error telling you to "drop the input and set asset_key". That hardened the **override** channel; `asset_key` itself still accepts whatever string arrives, so the derivation being "total for this writer" (`bugs_open/168`) is true of the *function* and not of its *input*.
- **THIS IS `bugs_open/248_…undeployed_asset_repair_deploys_every_asset_as_a_hero_under_a_placeholder_name.md`** — filed 2026-08-10, `090`-CONFIRMED, fix candidate 1 is "delete rung 2", one line. **Refer to it by SLUG: `248` is an ambiguous number.** This entry exists because the bug is OPEN and still firing, so a session touching an image deploy needs the check before it needs the case file.
- **the census in that bug UNDER-COUNTS, so do not size it from `assets`:** `filename LIKE '%asset-key%'` finds an instance only if the post-commit `assets`-row update ALSO took, and that update is best-effort (`deploy_image_asset_action.go:378-392`). The site that prompted this entry contributes **0 rows** while serving the 404 — all five of its hero rows have `filename = ''`. Ask the wire or the site repo. Re-measured on `updated_at` (not `created_at`, which the post-commit UPDATE makes meaningless here): **150 rows / 16 sites** on 2026-08-12, up from 118/10 on 08-10.
- **and check the RIGHT config key before believing it is fixed:** `asset-deployer.deploy_asset` `config.asset_key = "input_data.asset_key"` is rung 2 and was **still live 2026-08-12**. The `"asset_key?"` optional marker added elsewhere is on the CALLER's `input_mapping` and does not defuse it. Two spellings of one intent sit on this path — `input_data.asset_key` and `input_data.spec.asset_key` — so grepping the newer one and finding it correct proves nothing.
- **source:** `mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption` lane, 2026-08-12, owner reported "the hero image is no longer there". Generated 2026-08-11 12:45Z, live at the wrong URL (200, 68,984 bytes) ever since, work item `complete`; five heroes generated on that site that day, none reaching `/assets/images/hero.jpg`. Handoff §11.1, contribution written into 248. ⚠ I wrote this up as a fresh finding before grepping `/bugs_open/` — see `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-12.
- **added:** 2026-08-12, mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption lane

### Adding a domain to `sitesync`'s `DOMAINS` list delivers NOTHING until the git **sparse cone** includes it too — and the timer reports SUCCESS every 5 minutes while doing so

- **footprint:** `/usr/local/bin/sitesync` and `sitesync.service`/`.timer` on `webdesign.vs.mythic-beasts.com`; `/var/lib/sitesync/repo` (a `--filter=blob:none --sparse` clone); `gqls/vm-sites`; `docs024_key_docs_latest/webdesign_uk_build_service/box/setup-webdesignbox.sh:70`; `docs024_key_docs_latest/idea_uk_vm_site/box/provision-pullsync.sh:119`; any second domain added to a pull-sync box
- **fires when:** you host a second (or third) site on a pull-sync box and add it to the script's `DOMAINS` list, which reads like the whole change — the 2026-08-11 commit generalising `sitesync` from one hardcoded domain to a list even said so in its own NOTES. The **sparse cone is set in a different file that only ever runs once**, at provisioning: `git sparse-checkout set <domain>` — deliberately single-domain ("this box fetches ONLY idea.uk/"). `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/main` then succeed, materialise nothing for the new domain, and the repo folder never appears.
- **the tell: there is none, and three separate checks actively reassure you.** (1) `systemctl status sitesync.service` → `status=0/SUCCESS`, timer firing on schedule; (2) the box's checkout is at exactly the right commit and `git ls-tree origin/main` **does** list the new domain, so git plainly "has" it; (3) the files really are in the repo on GitHub, correct sizes and timestamps — so framework-side deploy verification passes completely. Measured 2026-08-12: `noted.co.uk`'s five pages committed to `gqls/vm-sites` 04:19–04:37, box at that exact commit, `/var/www/noted.co.uk` **empty** and nginx serving **403/162 B** eight hours later.
- **why it is silent rather than an error:** the script's own safety guard skips a missing folder by design — `if [ -d "$folder" ] && [ -d "$webroot" ]; then rsync …; fi`, added so that `set -e` plus rsync's exit 23 could not kill the timer and leave "sync silently stopped weeks ago". It is right for the case it was written for and **cannot distinguish "not deployed yet" from "sparse cone excludes it"**. Two lists that must agree, in two scripts, one never run again.
- **the check, one command, before believing any pull-sync delivery:** `git -C /var/lib/sitesync/repo sparse-checkout list` must contain **every** domain in the script's `DOMAINS`. Diff the two lists; do not eyeball one. Then verify at the web root, never at the unit: `ls /var/www/<domain>/` and a box-local `curl -H "Host: <domain>" http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` — **403 with an empty doc root is the signature**, and it is indistinguishable from a permissions problem if you only read the status.
- **the fix, and the hardening that ends the class:** `sudo -u www-data git -C /var/lib/sitesync/repo sparse-checkout add <domain>`. Better, since the drift pair is the actual defect: derive the cone **from `DOMAINS`** inside `sitesync` itself (`sparse-checkout set "${folders[@]}"` each run), so the two lists cannot disagree — or at minimum have the loop `echo` a warning when a configured domain has no repo folder, converting a silent skip into a visible one.
- **⚠ the repo is shared with a LIVE COMMERCIAL SHOPFRONT.** `sparse-checkout add` re-runs a checkout in the same clone that feeds `webdesign.uk`; a partial materialisation there would be propagated by the next `rsync -a --delete` into the live web root. Before/after control on the shopfront (box-local `Host: webdesign.uk` → `127.0.0.1:8080`, plus a file count) is mandatory, and note the recorded byte baseline drifts legitimately as that lane ships — compare against a reading you take yourself immediately before, not against a figure in a doc.
- **kin, not duplicate:** the `repo_name: "sites"` vs `vm-sites` entry above is "the commit landed in the wrong repo"; this one is "the commit landed in the RIGHT repo and the box will never check it out". Both end in "green everywhere, nothing served", which is why each needs its own check.
- **source:** `noted_rebuild/NOTES_noted_rebuild.md` 2026-08-12 12:40 (full working, incl. why populating the web root cannot disturb the live legacy app — the apex serves from B2, verified by `x-amz-*` headers)
- **added:** 2026-08-12, noted.co.uk rebuild lane

### The `content_duplication` fact-overlap count falls when a numeric fact's REGISTERED VALUE drifts — no repair required, and the number moves in the direction that looks like success

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/check_content_duplication.go` (`assignFacts`, `loadEvidenceFactIDs`, `containsStandalone`, `sharedFactCount`), `site_specs` aspect `evidence_base` (`facts[].value`), `site_work_items.spec->>'fact_overlap_pairs'` on `capability_gap:content_duplication_rewrite`, `stale_evidence` items, `bugs_open/151`, PBP-037
- **fires when:** you compare a site's `fact_overlap_pairs` figure against an earlier one — a before/after for a de-duplication fix, a trend read, or a "did the writer stop restating facts?" census. No symptom needed; the arithmetic is silent and it favours you.
- **the tell:** none in the count itself. The check assigns a fact to a section by finding the fact's **CURRENT registered value** as a standalone number in the section's **STORED text** (`containsStandalone(sections[i].Text, m.Value)`). Those are two different clocks. The evidence base is refreshed automatically — measured on fundamentallyai 2026-08-11→12, **four facts drifted overnight** (`F1-live-sites` 21→22, `F9` 9545→9706, `F10` 8297→8468, `F11` 244→266, `F12` 264→283) while not one page was rebuilt. Result: every chart section that still says "21" stopped matching `F1`, and each affected pair's shared-fact list quietly shrank by one. A pair sitting at exactly 3 shared facts **leaves the count entirely** on one drift, and the report reads as repair. The reverse also bites: a drift can push two sections to 3 shared facts and invent a pair.
- **the check:** pin the evidence base and reuse the SAME pinned copy for both halves of any comparison — dump `site_specs.data` once, measure before and after against that file, and say so where you record the figure. Then, before believing a movement, diff the values: `SELECT f->>'id', f->>'value' FROM site_specs, jsonb_array_elements(data->'facts') f WHERE site_id='<id>' AND aspect='evidence_base' AND is_current;` against your pinned dump. A `stale_evidence` item at `needs_human_review` (fundamentallyai has carried one all week) is a standing warning that this clock is moving. Also read the composition, never only the total: two censuses can both say 9 while naming different pairs, which is what surfaced this.
- **why it is a landmine and not a bug report:** the matcher is behaving as designed (a fact IS "stated" only if its current value appears), and no fix is obvious — matching stale values would report facts the site no longer claims. The defect is in **using the number as a time series**, which is exactly what a de-duplication programme does. The 2026-08-11 census that measured 34→9 on fundamentallyai is unaffected **because its before and after both used one pinned dump taken before any rebuild** — that was luck of method, not foresight, and it is the practice this entry asks for.
- **source:** 2026-08-11/12 fact-assignment census, `brochure_component_library/NOTES_brochure_component_library.md` (08-11 and 08-12 entries; the instrument is `fact_overlap_census.py`, a faithful port of the shipped check's fact half)
- **added:** 2026-08-12, brochure_component_library lane (fact-assignment front)

### Comparing a work item's flagged text against live copy PAGE-WIDE always finds it — the flagged token is often a bare number, and the false hit is indistinguishable from a real one

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/revalidate_unverified_claims.go` (`claimStillOnPage`, `flaggedClaimsFromSpec`), `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/check_unverified_claims.go` (`ClaimsPageScan.ExaminedTextBySlot`), `site_work_items.spec->'findings'` (`matched`, `snippet`, `slot_name`) for `item_type='claims_unverified'`, `page_components.rendered_html` / `content_data`, concept register CQ-021
- **fires when:** you ask "is the thing we flagged still on the page?" — auditing whether a revalidator closed items correctly, building any claim-granular gate, or checking a de-duplication or copy-fix by searching a stored finding's text against current copy. No symptom needed, and the obvious query (`... WHERE html ILIKE '%'||matched||'%'`) is the one that lies.
- **the tell: the AGGREGATE hides it completely; only the STRINGS show it.** `unregistered_number` and `unregistered_stat` findings cite the number itself, so `matched` is routinely **1–4 characters** — `5`, `26`, `50`, `97`, `100%`, `362`, `51%`. Those match a class name, an id, a price, a date or an unrelated figure somewhere in almost any page's markup. Measured 2026-08-11 across the 8 `auto:revalidated` items: **page-wide, 7 of 18 cited texts "still present"; scoped to the finding's own `slot_name`, 2.** Every one of the 7 was ≤4 chars; every distinctive token (`independently verified` 22 chars, `90,790+`, `3,419`, `7843`) was genuinely gone. A session reading `7 of 18` concludes the closures are defective, and nothing in that number can say otherwise.
- **the check:** scope to the slot the finding was raised in (`page_components.slot_name = spec->'findings'->>'slot_name'`), and **print `length(matched)` and the text itself beside the verdict** — never the bare count. A still-present column that is all tiny tokens while the absent column is all real phrases is the signature. Then ask the disconfirming question: a substring search for `5` returns "still present" on a page that was rewritten from scratch, so that check **could not have come out any other way**.
- **⚠ AND DO NOT "FIX" IT BY SWITCHING TO `snippet` — that fails in the OPPOSITE, UNSAFE direction.** The council seat that raised this asked for the cited *snippet* to be compared, which sounds strictly better. Measured against the demand control (items whose verdict is `still_holds`, where the claim is by definition still on the page): the slot-scoped **token** saw the claim in **40 of 41**; the slot-scoped **snippet** in **18 of 41**. A snippet is long enough that any whitespace or markup churn breaks the match — and in a gate, a missed match reads as *"the copy changed"*, which **grants closure**. Token over-fires (refuses, safe); snippet under-fires (closes, unsafe). **Pick the direction your failure mode lands in, and measure both against a population where you already know the answer.**
- **source:** `bugfix_168_deployed_asset_path/NOTES_deployed_asset_path.md` 2026-08-12; `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-12 (the near-miss: this was one step from being written up as "the gate would have refused 4 of 8 closures"); shipped in `58bede8d5`
- **added:** 2026-08-12, bugfix_168 retraction lane

### CLAUDE.md's owner rulings are INVISIBLE to council seats — cite one as your authority and the `prior_art_librarian` seat will gate on it, correctly

- **footprint:** `CLAUDE.md` (every "OWNER RULING" section), `doc_notes`, `scripts/landmines-sync.py`, `docs024_key_docs_latest/fixloop_eg_dartsonline/097_TRIGGER_council_review_v1.sh`, any council submission's `rationale`/`risks`/`grounded_in` that names a ruling
- **fires when:** you justify a change to the council by citing a CLAUDE.md owner ruling — the ordering exemption, the platform-seams rule, the 2026-08-02 opt-in-field rule, RFC_022's narrowing. This is the *normal* way to argue a submission, it is what CLAUDE.md tells you to rely on, and the seats cannot read it.
- **the tell:** none until the verdict. `prior_art_librarian` reads `doc_notes` and `diagnosis_artifacts`; its remit is unverified premises, and a policy citation it cannot retrieve is exactly its target. Measured 2026-08-12 (correlation `b67eb26a-…` round 6, a REVISE **gated** on this): the cited ruling is in `CLAUDE.md` (`grep -c "CONDITION (1) OF THE ORDERING EXEMPTION IS RETIRED"` → **1**) and has **ZERO** trace in `doc_notes` — `body ILIKE '%ordering exemption%'` → 0, `'%condition (1)%' AND '%retired%'` → 0, `'%after the fact, by design%'` → 0. The seat's objection was *"if that ruling does not exist or does not say what is claimed, the framing collapses"*, and on its own tooling that is unanswerable.
- **why it is structural, not a one-off:** `landmines-sync.py` syncs **LANDMINES.md** into `doc_notes` so seats can read it. **Nothing syncs CLAUDE.md's rulings.** So the corpus a submission is instructed to argue from is precisely the corpus its reviewers cannot see, and every lane citing a ruling inherits this.
- **⚠ the check that FAILS, and it is the obvious one:** `SELECT count(*) FROM doc_notes WHERE body ILIKE '%2026-07-29%'` returns **130** and reads as "the ruling is well recorded". It matches *the date string* — any note mentioning that day. **Query the ruling's distinctive WORDS, never its date**, and induce a zero you trust before believing a non-zero.
- **the check, before you submit:** grep your own submission for "ruling", "OWNER RULING" and any date-shaped authority, then for each one run a *word-based* `doc_notes` query. If it returns 0, either (a) get the ruling into `doc_notes` (a LANDMINES entry that states it, then `landmines-sync.py --apply`, is the only wired path today), or (b) mark it explicitly **UNVERIFIABLE FROM THIS SEAT'S TOOLING** and do not let it carry the argument's weight. Do NOT simply assert it harder — round 6 added a whole paragraph of ruling-citation to fix one seat's objection and drew a gating HIGH from another.
- **kin:** the sibling entry on `code_symbols` — same shape, different corpus (`prior_art_librarian` also cannot run `code_symbols`, so a producer count proved that way is unverifiable from that seat however sound the query).
- **source:** `bugfix_168_deployed_asset_path/NOTES_deployed_asset_path.md` 2026-08-12 (round 6 read-out); verdict in `diagnosis_artifacts` correlation `b67eb26a-14ef-45d7-b755-3e489fd57ef0`
- **added:** 2026-08-12, bugfix_168 retraction lane

### `ai_service.max_tokens` is read by `ExecuteAIStepAction`, NOT by the provider client — an action that calls `GenerateText` directly gets 2048 whatever the config says

- **⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-16 — THE HEADING ABOVE IS NOW HALF FALSE, and the entry is kept (not deleted) because the tell and the census method still earn their place.** `bugs_open/257` Path A moved budget resolution INTO the provider clients (`platform/aiservice/max_tokens.go`, `configMaxTokens`/`resolvedMaxTokens`/`DefaultMaxOutputTokens`; anthropic, gemini AND ollama). **A direct caller passing `nil` or `{}` now inherits `ai_service.max_tokens` from the config its CLIENT WAS CONSTRUCTED WITH**, and reaches the 2048 fallback only when nobody configured a budget anywhere. **NOT LIVE UNTIL THE NEXT ROLL** — Go is inert until an image ships, so until then read this entry exactly as originally written. Verify at the pod, per service, before relying on either version.
- **⚠ WHAT STILL BITES YOU AFTER THE FIX, and it is the half worth keeping:** a client is constructed from ONE config map, and **the STEP's own config is never passed to a constructor**. So `ai_actions.go:358-364`'s outer key (`agentConfig` — the AGENT's whole `default_config`) and `llmOptionsFromConfig`'s outer key (the STEP's config) still reach the API only through the options map. The fix closes "the configured budget silently became 2048"; it does NOT make a step-level budget arrive by itself. **`llmOptionsFromConfig` is still the right call**, for step config and for `budget_tokens`, which no constructor sees either.
- **⚠ the line numbers below are STALE and that is itself the lesson:** `anthropic.go:109`/`:147` moved to `:185`/`:280-281` when `bugs_open/244`'s prompt-caching work landed, and the 2048 is now the named constant `aiservice.DefaultMaxOutputTokens`. The filing quoted coordinates; coordinates rot. Grep the symbol, not the line.
- **⚠ the census below (9 sites, 2026-08-12) was already stale by 2026-08-16 — 10 sites.** `internal/tools-api/handlers/gripper.go:161` arrived in between (commit `f967d9307`), and `gemini.go` carried the SAME hardcoded 2048 all along and is absent from the original census entirely, because that session read one client. **Re-run the grep; never quote a call-site census you did not run today.**
- **⚠ `reasoning-agent`, named below as hard-pinned and unconfigurable, is NOT a live burn — measured 2026-08-16.** 3 replicas `1/1 Running`, entire log is startup, zero request-handling lines, zero `TruncatedError`; and `grep -rn "system.agent.reasoning.requests"` finds the consumer plus ONE hardcoded "known topics" list in `core-manager/admin/system_handlers.go:132`. **No producer exists.** A deployed service consuming a topic nothing writes to. Do not re-file it as an outage. (Its `ai_service.max_tokens: 2048` is now live but also needs ITS OWN image roll — it is not the chassis.)
- **footprint:** `platform/aiservice/anthropic.go:109` (`"max_tokens": 2048`), `anthropic.go:147` · `platform/orchestration/actions/ai_actions.go:358-364` · any `.GenerateText(` / `.GenerateWithImages(` call outside `ExecuteAIStepAction` · `agent_definitions` `default_config->'workflow'->'steps'->*->'config'->'ai_service'->'max_tokens'` · `llm_call_log`
- **fires when:** you set or raise `max_tokens` on a step and re-run, or you write a new action that calls a provider client directly because it needs a one-off completion. The config key is real, documented, correctly nested and at the right path — and it reaches the API only if the call goes through `ExecuteAIStepAction`, which is the single place that translates it into the `options` map the client actually reads. `GenerateText` accepts `nil`, so nothing complains.
- **the tell:** the error echoes back the OLD number. Measured 2026-08-10: after migration 372 set `max_tokens: 8000` on a live step, the very next failure still said `output_tokens=2048 reached the configured cap`. That reads as "still too small" and it means "your number never left the building" — the filing session changed live config a SECOND time before opening the call site. **A value the error repeats unchanged after you have changed it is the signature of a key nothing reads, and no further config change can help.** Second concealment: these calls write **no `llm_call_log` row** (that table is written by the function being bypassed), so the fleet's own "which steps truncate" instrument is blind to exactly the calls most likely to — `agent_type ILIKE '%reason%'` returns **0 rows** for a deployed, running service.
- **the check:** before editing config, `grep -n "GenerateText(" <the action's file>` and read what is passed as the third argument. `map[string]interface{}{}` or `nil` means the config is inert and the edit is wasted. Census of every direct call site, which the code index CANNOT answer (it does not index function bodies, so a content search returns 0 regardless): `grep -rn "\.GenerateText(\|\.GenerateWithImages(" --include=*.go platform/ internal/ cmd/ | grep -v _test.go | grep -v platform/aiservice/`. Run 2026-08-12 it found **9 call sites, one passing `nil`** — `internal/agents/reasoning/agent.go:127`, a deployed service with **zero** occurrences of `max_tokens` in its file, hard-pinned at 2048 and unconfigurable.
- **source:** `bugs_open/257` (the class + the census) · `bugs_open/205` (the unconfigured instance) · council `65d153f0`, where four seats independently objected that the contract has one entry point and using it is optional · reproduction in `provocation_pipeline/NOTES_provocation_pipeline.md` 2026-08-10
- **added:** 2026-08-12, provocation_pipeline lane

### `hasActiveAssetForPurpose` returns true for an UNRELATED page-variant asset — "does the canonical fallback have an asset" needs `hasActiveAssetForAssetKey`

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/imagery_helpers.go` (`hasActiveAssetForPurpose`, `hasActiveAssetForAssetKey`), `check_placeholder_image_in_use.go` (the canonical-fallback gate), any check asking "does THE site's logo/hero exist" rather than "does any asset of this purpose exist", `assets.purpose` vs `assets.asset_key`
- **fires when:** a site has page-named imagery variants (`hero_about`, `hero_contact`, …) alongside the canonical `hero`/`logo`. Both share `purpose='hero'`; only the canonical row has `asset_key='hero'`. A check that asks `hasActiveAssetForPurpose(site, 'hero')` gets **true** the moment ANY variant is active, even if the canonical fallback asset was deleted, tombstoned, or never existed — silently treating "some hero image exists somewhere" as "the fallback path is resolved".
- **the tell: none at the call site** — the function name reads correctly ("has active asset for purpose... hero... yes") and the sibling function `hasActiveAssetForAssetKey` **already has a doc comment warning about exactly this** ("post Phase 2D, multiple active rows can share a purpose... use hasActiveAssetForAssetKey when checking whether a SPECIFIC image variant is present"), so the trap is fully documented one function away and still bit code written after that comment existed. Measured 2026-08-12: `hasActiveAssetForPurpose(mortgagecalculator, 'hero')` → **true** (2 active rows: `hero_about`, `hero_contact`) while `hasActiveAssetForAssetKey(mortgagecalculator, 'hero')` → **false** (0 rows — the canonical hero was superseded). A discovery check gated on the first call silently stopped re-detecting a real, still-open gap on six live pages, directly defeating an explicit "keep this live for redetection" instruction.
- **the check:** before gating on "does an asset exist" for a CANONICAL slot (logo, hero — where `asset_key == purpose` by convention), always use `hasActiveAssetForAssetKey(dctx, purpose)`, never `hasActiveAssetForPurpose`. Reserve the latter for a genuinely purpose-wide question ("has this site generated ANY icon, regardless of which one") — which none of the current discovery checks actually ask.
- **UPDATE 2026-08-12 — council's `bug_historian` seat objected (advisory, medium) that the fix's own audit was scoped to `discovery_checks/` only, naming `image-build-handler` and `check_undeployed_assets.go` by name as unaudited possible second call sites. Answered with a wider grep rather than argument: `grep -rn hasActiveAssetForPurpose platform/ internal/ pkg/ cmd/` returns **only the function's own definition** — zero remaining callers anywhere, in ANY package. Both named suspects are cleared structurally, not just empirically: the function takes `DiscoveryCheckContext`, a type private to `discovery_checks`, so `image-build-handler` (a different package) cannot call it at all; `check_undeployed_assets.go` was checked directly and has no bare `purpose`-only `assets` query. Separately swept all five `discovery_checks/*.go` files that query `FROM assets` for the SAME PATTERN under a different name (a purpose-only filter with no `asset_key` constraint) — none found. The objection is answered, not merely noted: this was structurally the only instance, fleet-wide, at the time of the fix.**
- **source:** 2026-08-12, `bugfix_210_needs_logo_unhandleable` lane, found while verifying the owner's own "keep it live" instruction actually held; council corr `7e839679-d87b-4c57-9419-ba1212f22a87`, APPROVED
- **added:** 2026-08-12, bugfix_210_needs_logo_unhandleable lane

### A hook's `additionalContext` delivery is NOT in `toolUseResult` — any sweep that measures "did the session see it?" from stdout scores every out-of-band delivery as a MISS

- **footprint:** `scripts/advisory-delivery-sweep.py` · `scripts/commit-advisory-postuse.py` · `scripts/landmines-session-start.py` · `scripts/memory-index.py` · `.claude/hooks/psql_readonly_gate.py` · `.claude/settings.json` (any `PostToolUse`/`SessionStart` matcher) · `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` · `~/.claude/projects/-home-ant-projects-agentchassis/*.jsonl` (`toolUseResult.stdout`, `attachment.stdout`) · concept register OPP-005, OPP-007
- **fires when:** you write, run or quote any measurement of whether a hook's output actually reached a session — a delivery sweep, an adoption count, a verify-later on a hook you just shipped. It also fires the moment you *move* a signal out of band: the instrument that measured the old channel keeps working, keeps passing its controls, and silently stops being able to see success.
- **the tell: the number moves the WRONG WAY after a fix that works.** Measured 2026-08-12: `advisory-delivery-sweep.py --since 2026-08-12` reported **38.2% delivered, below its own 55% pre-fix baseline**, for a window whose true figure was **100% (36/36)** — 23 of those reached the session *only* via the hook. The sweep tested `"commit scope:" in toolUseResult.stdout`; `additionalContext` is never in `toolUseResult`.
