Evidence survives on the row ONLY for arms that leave the item at a status `complete_work_item`'s guard excludes (`needs_human_review`, `failed`, …) — parked rows keep their `result_fields` + `error`, completed rows do not. Design accordingly: park-evidence on the row, close-evidence in the orchestration trail, and never assert a completed row's route from `result`.
- **source:** 2026-08-15, bugfix_277 lane (seed 410 canary; RUNBOOK corrected the same hour). The loop behaviour is pre-existing (`051_build_dispatch_loop.sql` `mark_complete`), not 277's.
- **added:** 2026-08-15, bugfix_277 lane

### gofmt REWRITES two single quotes in a Go doc comment into a typographic ” — SQL quoted in a comment is silently mangled

- **footprint:** `gofmt`, `gofmt -w`, any Go DOC comment (the `//` block directly above a declaration) that quotes SQL or code containing `''` (an empty string literal, e.g. `COALESCE(col, '')`) or ``` `` ```
- **fires when:** you paste a SQL predicate into a doc comment to explain a helper — `COALESCE(build_status,'') <> 'deployed'` — and the pre-commit pattern check reports the file `not gofmt-clean`. You run `gofmt -w` as instructed. Go 1.19+ doc-comment reformatting treats `` `` `` and `''` as TeX-style quotes and converts them to “ and ”, so the comment now reads `COALESCE(build_status,”) <> 'deployed'` — SQL that will not run if anyone copies it, in a comment whose whole purpose was to be copied.
- **the tell:** none in the loop — `go build`, `go vet`, `go test` all pass; the gofmt "diff" is one character wide and looks like a whitespace fix. Seen 2026-08-15 on two files in one commit; noticed only because `gofmt -d` was read before `gofmt -w`.
- **the check:** `gofmt -d <file>` (read the diff) before `gofmt -w` (apply it) whenever the flagged file's change was a COMMENT. If the diff touches a `''` or ``` `` ```, do not apply — rewrite the prose instead: put the SQL in an indented code block inside the comment (gofmt leaves indented blocks alone), or spell the empty string as `<empty>` in running text. Body-of-code string literals are untouched; only doc comments are reformatted.
- **relations:** the struct-field-comment gofmt landmine above (same tool, different rewrite); `016b §9 #16`
- **source:** 2026-08-15, 185 closing lane, `41f88f2b3` (comments rewritten to `<empty>`)
- **added:** 2026-08-15, bugfix bugs_open/185 lane

### `{{.ComponentID}}` is the estate's per-instance id convention on ONE render path and the component's SHARED id on the other — adopt it for reuse and you may namespace nothing at all

- **footprint:** `{{.ComponentID}}` in any `content_components.html_template` · `platform/orchestration/actions/assemble_from_library.go:277,291` · `platform/orchestration/actions/v3_site_actions.go:2055` (`RenderComponentAction`) · `faq`, `generic-text-block`, `mechanism-flow`, `evidence-timeseries`, `pricing` (the components already using it) · any change whose purpose is placing one component on a page TWICE
- **fires when:** you set out to make a component safe to instantiate more than once on a page, find that the platform already has a convention for unique element ids, and adopt it — `id="{{.ComponentID}}-loanAmount"`. It renders. The id is visibly templated, not literal. Nothing errors. On the `RenderComponentAction` path both instances still receive **the same** value, so the ids are byte-identical and every `getElementById` still resolves to the first copy — i.e. you have done the work, produced a templated-looking artefact, and fixed nothing.
- **the mechanism, measured 2026-08-15:** the two paths substitute different things and the values are not even the same shape. `assemble_from_library.go:277` builds `componentID := fmt.Sprintf("component_%s_%d", comp.Function, idx)` — the loop index makes it unique **per instance on the page**, so reuse is genuinely safe there. `v3_site_actions.go:2055` does `renderCtx.ContentData["ComponentID"] = comp.ID`, which is the **`content_components` row id** — one value shared by every instance of that component, and a UUID (`uuid.Parse(comp.ID)` at `:2106`) rather than a `component_<function>_<n>` string. Both are reached through `{{.ComponentID}}`; only one of them namespaces anything.
- **why the wrong result looks exactly right:** on a page with **one** instance — which is every page using these five components today — the two paths are indistinguishable, because uniqueness is untested when there is nothing to collide with. A single-instance canary therefore passes under either substitution. The defect only appears at the second instance, which is the case you were trying to enable.
- **the check:** before trusting the convention, establish which path renders the page you care about, then assert the value **differs between two instances** rather than that it is present: render a two-instance page and `grep -o 'id="[^"]*"' | sort | uniq -d` — it must print **nothing**. A test asserting the id merely *contains* a substitution passes in both worlds and is not a test. Never infer per-instance uniqueness from a template that reads `{{.ComponentID}}`; that string is a request, and what it resolves to is a property of the renderer.
- **the general form:** a shared placeholder name is not a shared guarantee. When two code paths both honour a template variable, the variable's NAME is the thing they agree on; its SEMANTICS can differ, and nothing in the template surface shows you which one you are getting.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/283` (the filing this came from — 173 of 240 active components hardcode an element id, 166 literal-only, 100 bind by `getElementById`, so this is the fix path for the whole class) · MEMORY [[a-doc-comment-is-not-an-enforcement-mechanism]] (same shape: a declaration that looks like a control) · [[writes-the-field-is-not-reads-the-field]] · [[a-guarantee-conditional-on-a-classifier-inherits-its-gaps]]
- **⚠ UPDATE 2026-08-16 — there is now a real per-instance value, and this entry's advice is "use THAT", not "measure ComponentID more carefully".** `{{.InstanceID}}` (register **CLC-014**, commits `03c1b0b90` + `32d6e980a`) is bound on **every** render path that renders a page-embedded component, from one rule: the component **function** plus its **occurrence** on the page — `c-mortgages-repayment`, `c-mortgages-repayment-2`. Bind it via `BindInstanceToken` / `BindSingleSectionInstanceToken`; `scripts/pattern-check.py`'s `check_unscoped_component_render` fires on a new render call site that binds neither. **`{{.ComponentID}}` is deliberately UNCHANGED** — re-pointing it would move the served element ids of the five live components that use it, which is architecture-scope, and it is filed as the follow-up the council's architecture seat asked for. So everything above still holds for `ComponentID`; it is simply no longer the thing you should reach for. The `[UNVERIFIED]` in the source line below is **CLOSED** (283 §8.1, 2026-08-15) — and it closed the unsafe way, which is why the seam was built.
- **⚠ and the near-miss worth carrying:** the first version of `InstanceID` shipped a second helper, `InstanceTokenFromSlot`, for the path that could not see the page — same key, weaker guarantee, different shape. That is **this landmine's own shape, recreated one day later, in the change written to fix it**, by the person who wrote this entry. The council's `reuse_agent` seat caught it; the helper is deleted. A new name does not make a second guarantee safe — the trap is two guarantees reachable through one key, whatever the key is called.
- **source:** 2026-08-15, LMC Track B2 lane, filing `bugs_open/283` after the reuse demonstration had to be run on its own page. Both injection sites read first-hand in the Go source; the `[UNVERIFIED]` half — which path serves a `page_rerender` on these pages — is stated as open in 283 §4 rather than guessed, and is exactly what makes this a landmine rather than a solved problem.
- **added:** 2026-08-15, loanandmortgagecalculator_couk lane; **updated 2026-08-16** (283 round 2)

### Adding a directory kind in Go publishes NOTHING until the publish trigger's SQL VALUES mapping gains its row — and every check you'd naturally run says the kind is live

- **footprint:** `directoryPublishProfiles` (`platform/orchestration/actions/render_directory_action.go`) · `model-directory-trigger` (`agent_definitions.default_config`, `find_directory_sites` query) · `SEED_directory_publish_trigger.sql` · any new register kind (`directory_entities.kind`)
- **fires when:** you add a seventh directory kind. The Go side is a closed profile set (`directoryPublishProfiles`), so you add the profile, the components row, the opt-in spec key, the checks enablement, the planner vocabulary — six places, all Go-or-data, and DIR-001 used to say six is all of them. Since migration 429 (2026-08-15) there is a SEVENTH: the publish trigger's find-sites query carries the kind→spec_key→snippet/listing-components→commit-message mapping as a SQL `VALUES` list in `agent_definitions`, in deliberate lockstep with the Go set. A kind absent from that list is never found DUE, so it never publishes.
- **why the wrong result looks right:** nothing errors and everything you'd check reads healthy — the researcher registers claims, `render_directory` renders the kind on demand (probe it manually and it works), the trigger completes green every 6h (your kind simply isn't in its result set), and the scheduled task stamps `last_completed_at` on time. The absence is only visible as "the site repo never gains `data/<kind>-….json`", which reads as "pages not built yet" for weeks.
- **the check:** when adding a kind, grep the LIVE trigger row for it — `SELECT position('<kind>' IN default_config#>>'{workflow,steps,find_directory_sites,config,query}') FROM agent_definitions WHERE type='model-directory-trigger' AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL;` — non-zero or you are not done. Update the row by snapshot-first migration (429 is the worked example) AND sync `SEED_directory_publish_trigger.sql` in the same commit.
- **relations:** DIR-001 (the SEVEN-places note) · [[dedup-index-go-list-lockstep]] (same contract shape: SQL artefact ↔ Go closed set) · FINDING_2026-08-10 in `model_directory_pipeline/` (how the previous publish-leg absence hid for 15 days)
- **source:** 2026-08-15, portfolio_positioning Phase B3c — the lockstep was created knowingly (deriving the mapping at run time needs a Go roll; B3c was config-only by design) and this entry is the stated cost.
- **added:** 2026-08-15, portfolio_positioning lane

### A `component_versions` row labelled "Regenerated by component-creator" is the template that was REPLACED, not the regen's output — read the direction before calling any version "the recovery"

- **footprint:** `component_versions` (`changed_by='component-creator:regen'`, `change_description='Regenerated by component-creator'`; likewise `update_component_html` "Pre-edit snapshot" and `repair_template_slots`) · `store_generated_component_action.go` `snapshotComponentVersion` · any incident timeline built from `component_versions`
- **fires when:** you reconstruct what a shared component's template was at time T from its version rows and read `vN` as "the state written at `vN.created_at`". Every writer in this estate snapshots the CURRENT template immediately BEFORE its UPDATE (`store_generated_component_action.go:439-451`; `update_component_html_action.go` step 2), so `vN` is the state that ENDED at `created_at`, and the state that BEGAN there is only visible as `v(N+1)` or the live row.
- **why the wrong result looks right:** the description says "Regenerated" and the timestamp is the regen's, so a 7,714-char row reads as "the regen produced a 7,714-char template". On `a7daa5c5…` that reading made the 2026-08-05 POISON (v2: "Developer Resource Library", no `{{.body}}`) look like the recovery, and bug 285 + TL-042 published it that way ("recovery-by-coincidence").
- **the check:** `SELECT version_number, changed_by, length(html_template), html_template LIKE '%{{.%' FROM component_versions WHERE component_id=… ORDER BY 1` and read each row as *the pre-state of the write named in `changed_by`*; the post-state of the LAST write is the live `content_components.html_template`. When you need "what was live between v2 and v3", that is v3's html, not v2's.
- **relations:** bugs_open/285 (mis-read there 2026-08-15, corrected the same day) · TL-042 · bugs_closed/012 (the writer whose snapshot convention this is)
- **added:** 2026-08-15, bugfix_285_shared_template_write lane

### A live agent PROMPT still asks the LLM for `content_guidance`, so grep says the key is live — but on a work ITEM spec only `suggestion` is ever read

- **footprint:** `site_work_items.spec` steering keys (`suggestion`, `content_guidance`) · `platform/orchestration/actions/load_work_item_actions.go` (`aliasGuidanceIntoSuggestion`) · `platform/orchestration/actions/apply_gap_plan_action.go` (both the plan READ at :178 and the item-spec write) · `agent_definitions` rows `content-gap-planner`, `page-build-handler`, `page-content-writer` · any new producer of `content_rewrite` / `needs_content_page` items
- **fires when:** you write a work item that carries a brief — "state X, remove Y, add Z" — and reach for a key name. `content_guidance` is the obvious one: it reads like the field for guidance, four Go emitters used it, and grepping the live config finds it **in `content-gap-planner`'s own prompt**, which looks exactly like a live consumer. It is not: that hit is the agent's instruction to the LLM to emit the key into its PLAN. On an item spec the only key any reader reads is **`suggestion`** — `page-build-handler` maps `"rewrite_guidance?": "input_data.spec.suggestion"` and `page-content-writer` renders it under `## Rewrite Guidance`.
- **why the wrong result looks exactly right:** nothing errors and the work still happens. The item is claimed, the page is rewritten fluently, the item reports `complete`, and the page looks fine — it was just written to no instruction, steered by `evidence_base.writer_block` and the existing copy. The failure is **intermittent by construction**: a brief that restates what the register already says appears to work, so the channel seems flaky rather than dead. Measured cost before anyone noticed: four LLM rewrite rounds on one FAQ answer (`bugs_open/271` §1), three of them spent "fixing" register defects the rounds appeared to expose.
- **the check:** never infer a reader from a config `LIKE` hit — follow it to the step that consumes it. To ask what actually reads an item-spec key, search the whole config text (a structured `jsonb_each` over `workflow->steps` sees neither prompt text nor anything inside a loop's `sub_workflow`, and returns a confident, incomplete answer): `SELECT type FROM agent_definitions WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL AND default_config::text LIKE '%spec.<key>%';` For `spec.suggestion` that is exactly three rows (`page-build-handler`, `content-gap-planner`, `css-patch-agent`); for `spec.content_guidance` it is **zero**. Then verify at the artefact, not the config: grep `llm_call_log.prompt_rendered` for a sentinel phrase from your brief.
- **since 9a7d23c49 (2026-08-15) a guidance-only spec is ALIASED at the loader, which changes the trap rather than removing it:** `aliasGuidanceIntoSuggestion` fills `suggestion` from `content_guidance` in memory at dispatch, so a brief under the old name now reaches the writer — **but only once a chassis roll carries that commit, and only for items that pass through `LoadWorkItemsAction`.** The DB row is never rewritten, so `spec` in the table still shows the old key and a SQL-only reader sees no change. Write `suggestion`; the alias is a safety net for producers nobody can edit (config-driven `create_work_item`, operator SQL), not a licence to keep using the dead name.
- **the general form:** a key's presence in live config proves a WRITER exists, never a reader — and the two can be different layers of the same agent. When a channel seems to work sometimes, suspect a second channel doing the work rather than an unreliable first one.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/271` · register **WDS-016** (the seam, and the never-mutate exception it narrows) · **WDS-014** (`setRoutingField`, same root constraint: `input_mapping` has no coalesce syntax) · MEMORY [[writes-the-field-is-not-reads-the-field]] · [[grep-the-config-key-before-calling-it-a-win]] · [[a-config-key-that-nothing-reads]] · `bugs_open/279` (`work_item_type`: the same false-affordance shape on the same table)
- **added:** 2026-08-15, bugfix_271_content_guidance lane

### The all-zeros sha is git's NULL-SHA CONSTANT and is genuinely embedded in git-aware Go binaries — as a binary-probe negative control it fires "CONTROL-BROKEN" on a probe that is actually fine

- **footprint:** `grep -aq <sha> /proc/1/exe` deploy verification (the recipe in CLAUDE.md "Building & deploying" and any doc that copies it) · `docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/422_site_publish_reconciler_HOLD.sql` header (carried the bad control until 2026-08-15) · any binary built from code that imports git plumbing
- **fires when:** you follow "always run a control in the same breath — a sha that must be absent" and pick `0000000000000000000000000000000000000000` as the must-be-absent value, because it looks like the obviously-impossible sha.
- **why the wrong result looks right:** the control MATCHES (the binary really does contain forty consecutive zeros — git's null-sha literal, present in any binary that speaks git), so the probe reports itself broken and the true positive result you already have ("stamp sha matched, sibling shas did not") reads as untrustworthy. Measured on agent-chassis v1.0.1303, 2026-08-15: zero-sha matched; a random 40-hex value (`7f3a9c2e8b1d…`) did not; the stamp probe correctly discriminated 1 of 4 candidate shas. The failure direction is a STALL — a held seed or a verified deploy waits on a probe that was never broken.
- **the check:** the negative control must be a RANDOM 40-hex value, never the null sha and never any string with a plausible reason to exist. If the random value matches, the probe is genuinely non-discriminating (Go digit-table class); if only the zero-sha matches, the probe is fine and you have just found git's constant.
- **relations:** the "never a *discovery* grep for some 40-hex string" entry above (same probe, different failure); `bugs_open/153` (the provenance stamp this probe verifies)
- **verification:** settled first-hand by the filing session, 2026-08-15, all four probes run against live pod `agent-chassis-584b6fcf-9mtqd` (`/proc/1/exe`, v1.0.1303) and quoted above: zero-sha → match; random hex → no match; stamp sha `5e075a6f9…` → match on both replicas; three sibling commit shas → no match. The discrimination is the proof the probe works and the zero-sha match is a constant, not a broken probe.
- **added:** 2026-08-15, site_delivery_and_editor lane (hit while executing the 422 seed's own header recipe, which prescribed the bad control — header fixed in the same session)

### A `nav_drift` rebuild updates the stored chrome on EVERY page and redeploys only SOME — so the DB reads 100% clean while most of the live site is stale

- **footprint:** `site_work_items` `item_type='nav_drift'`, `nav-updater`, `pages.rendered_footer`, `pages.rendered_header`, `pages.rendered_head`, `site_components` (`footer-theme-chrome`, `header-theme-chrome`), any nav/footer/header membership change
- **fires when:** you change nav membership (`pages.in_header` / `in_footer`) and fire the `nav_drift` → `nav-updater` path that CLAUDE.md names — i.e. the correct, documented procedure, followed correctly. It completes, and it genuinely works.
- **the tell: the obvious verification query says the job is DONE, and it is wrong.** Measured 2026-08-15 on dartsonline.com after removing `Shipping & Returns` from the footer — the item reached `complete`, and:
  ```sql
  -- pages whose STORED footer still carries the removed link
  SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE rendered_footer ILIKE '%shipping-returns%') FROM pages …;
  -- 0 of 25.  Every stored footer correct.
  ```
  Then the served fleet, same moment: **19 of 25 pages still shipped the old footer.** Only 6 had been redeployed. The gap is **deploy, not render** — the rebuild refreshed all 25 stored chromes and pushed a subset to the site repo, and nothing anywhere reports the difference.
- **why the sample nearly hid it:** the 6 that WERE clean include `index.html`, `/guides/index.html` and `/news/index.html` — the pages a person spot-checks first. My first check was the homepage alone and read as a complete success. It was `/about.html` and `/contact.html`, checked only because a footer is on every page, that broke the story. **Check a page nobody would think to check, and check by count over the whole sitemap, not by eye over the obvious three.**
- **the check:** never grade a chrome change at `pages.rendered_*`. Enumerate the site's active URLs and grep the SERVED bytes:
  ```bash
  urls=$(psql -t -A -c "SELECT p.url FROM pages p JOIN sites s ON s.id=p.site_id
                         AND s.domain='<domain>' WHERE p.status='active';")
  for u in $urls; do printf "%s %s\n" "$u" \
      "$(curl -s "https://<domain>$u" | grep -c '<the string that should be gone>')"; done
  ```
  Then republish the stragglers with an **assemble-only** `page_rerender` — spec `{domain, page_id, page_name, filename}` and **no `reason` key** (3,287 such items have completed in 30 days). Assemble-only is right here precisely because the stored chrome is already correct: it re-concatenates and deploys without regenerating anything, so it cannot escalate to the content writer the way `reason=section_data_resolved` can on a page with a NULL `content_data` section.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/117` (chrome is a stored artefact) states the render half of this; this entry is the **deploy** half, which 117 does not cover · MEMORY `a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact` and `prove-a-deploy-at-the-artefact-index` (same family: a terminal status is not an artefact) · the `page_id`-not-`page_name` trap on the same action
- **added:** 2026-08-15

### tools-api's second tool splits ONE path prefix across TWO gin groups — put the cluster's `/requests` in the CORS group and every pull 403s; put a browser route in the internal-key group and the intake is open to the internet — and both mistakes look like a working router

- **footprint:** `internal/tools-api/api/server.go` (`mountGripper`) · `internal/tools-api/middleware/internalkey.go` · `internal/tools-api/middleware/cors.go` · any third tool added under `/api/v1/tools/<name>` · `platform/orchestration/actions/ndjson_feed.go` (the caller that sends only `X-Internal-Key`, no `Origin`)
- **fires when:** you add a route to tools-api by copying the nearest block. The gauntlet group has ONE middleware chain (`CORSMiddleware` → limiter → cap) and every route hangs off it, so the obvious move for a new endpoint is `apiGroup.GET(...)`. For a browser route that is right. For a route the CLUSTER calls it is a silent lockout: `CORSMiddleware` resolves `Origin` against the island `sites` table and answers `403 origin not allowed` when there is none — and a server-to-server GET has none. `pull_report_requests` treats any non-200 as a whole-site failure, logs a warning nobody reads, and returns `nil` error with `sites_err=1`; the task keeps ticking green.
- **the inverse is worse and equally quiet:** register `/session` or `/submit` on the internal-key group and CORS never runs — the response carries no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so a *browser* on robot-hands.com is refused by its own CORS check (looks like the same 403-class failure from the front)… while `curl` from anywhere, with a made-up key header, is refused by `InternalKey` — and with NO key requirement (a route on neither group) it simply works for the whole internet. `TestGripperRequestsIsNotBehindCORS` and `TestGripperGroupIsOptIn` pin the split for the four routes that exist; they do not know about the fifth.
- **the check:** before registering a route, name its CALLER. Browser → the CORS group (`pub` in `mountGripper`); cluster/mesh → the internal-key group (`internal`), and NOTHING goes on the bare engine. Then prove it at the socket, both directions: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST <host>/api/v1/tools/gripper/session` (no Origin) must be **403**; the same with `-H 'Origin: https://robot-hands.com'` must be **200**; `curl -s -w '%{http_code}' <host>/api/v1/tools/gripper/requests` must be **401**, and with the right `X-Internal-Key` **200** with an NDJSON body ending in a `{"_meta":…}` line. A pull that "works" from a browser tab is the bug.
- **two neighbours in the same lane, recorded here because they mislead before any symptom:** (1) **the island `sites` table has NO `deploy_config` column** — it is `island_db_prep.sql`'s minimal id/domain/status table — so `PROPOSAL_2026-08-05 §4`'s "check the key against `sites.deploy_config->'report_island'->>'pull_key'`" is a query that cannot run on the box that serves the route; the key is `GRIPPER_PULL_KEY` in `/opt/island/.env` and must be pasted equal to what seed 208 writes on the CLUSTER. Grep `\d sites` on the island before believing any column name carried over from clients_db. (2) **the intake's spec must speak the CLUSTER's field names**, not `DESIGN §2`'s: the live `report-builder` `load_request` step reads `spec->>'mass_kg'`, `'travel_mm'`, `'surface_material'`, `'ip_min'`, … and there is no renaming step between `/requests` and `score_grippers`. `gripper.Fields` + `TestFieldNamesAreTheClustersVocabulary` hold the line; if you "correct" a name to match the design doc, the pipeline fails on `mass_kg is required` after the visitor has already been promised an email.
- **relations:** register **PUB-005** (the seam) · **PUB-002** (`Limiter`/`CheckIntake` — first consumers here) · `robot_hands_gripper_dossier/PROPOSAL_2026-08-05_…` §4 (corrected by neighbour 1) · `DESIGN_2026-07-24 §5.3` (corrected by neighbour 2) · MEMORY [[a-client-side-absence-is-not-an-absence]] (a guard only guards the door you walk through)
- **added:** 2026-08-16, gripper dossier lane (while building the route group; the CORS-vs-key split was reasoned out BEFORE the first curl, the two neighbours were found by reading the island prep and the live workflow row)

### `spec_data` on `create_work_item` is a PATH STRING — pass it as an inline `{key: path}` MAP and every item files with `spec = '{}'`, the seed-time strict check passes, and the item reads as filed

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/create_work_item_action.go` (`spec_data` / `spec_paths` / `spec_literal`) · `platform/orchestration/datahelpers/action_inputs.go` (`ExtractActionInputs` Strategy 0/4/5) · any `agent_definitions` step whose `action` is `create_work_item` — especially one COPIED from `tool-auditor.create_items_loop.create_improve_item` before migration 434 · every consumer that reads `input_data.spec.<key>` (e.g. `tool-improver.load_tool` → `spec.page_id`, the build-dispatch-loop's `issue? <- current_item.spec.issue`)
- **fires when:** you author or copy a `create_work_item` step and write the spec the way it READS naturally: `"spec_data": {"page_id": "tool_data.page_id", "issue": "current_finding.description"}`. That is exactly the contract of `spec_paths`. `spec_data` is a single path to a map already in collected data; a map VALUE resolves through no strategy (0 and 4 want strings, 5 deliberately leaves composites alone), so `GetMap("spec_data")` is nil and the spec is `{}`. The bugs_open/234 strict check validates KEY NAMES, not value types, so seed time is silent; the item inserts fine; the failure surfaces LATER as a downstream `query param path 'input_data.spec.page_id' resolved to nil` in a DIFFERENT agent — and if nothing downstream reads the spec, never. Measured 2026-08-15: **233/233** `audit_fix` improve_tool items ever filed had no `spec.page_id`; four live producers (tool-auditor ×2, internal-linker, component-quality-auditor) had shipped this way for weeks. Note the failure mode is the SAME as retired-key `spec` (234) with a different spelling — the register/234 text describes it and it recurred anyway.
- **the check:** before seeding, type-census the step: `SELECT jsonb_typeof(steps.value->'config'->'spec_data') FROM agent_definitions, jsonb_each(default_config->'workflow'->'steps') steps WHERE …` (and again over `config->'sub_workflow'->'steps'`) — anything but `string` is the bug. After the FIRST live run, read one filed item: `SELECT spec FROM site_work_items WHERE item_key LIKE '<prefix>%' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1` — `{}` is the tell. Migration 434 converted the four; the pattern is `spec_paths` for references (unresolved = hard error, by design) + `spec_literal` for constants. **Do not put LLM-optional fields in `spec_paths`** (an absent optional key fails the whole item); leave them out unless a live consumer reads them.
- **relations:** bugs_open/234 (the retired `spec` key — same outcome, one spelling over) · bugs_open/024 (why `spec_paths` hard-errors) · seed `434_spec_data_map_is_never_read_four_producers_file_empty_specs.sql` · MEMORY [[writes-the-field-is-not-reads-the-field]], [[a-config-key-that-nothing-reads]]
- **added:** 2026-08-16, webdesign_tool_rebuilds lane (found while backfilling two "gap-shape" improve_tool items whose spec turned out to be empty for EVERY item the producer had ever filed, not a two-item window)

### A `section_edit` on a per-site TOOL FORK whose template carries `{{.field}}` copy and whose `content_data` is `{}` re-renders every text node to EMPTY — the class-attribute floors PASS (every class survives), the item completes, and the raw-tag check reads clean because there is nothing left to be raw

- **footprint:** `section_edit` / `content_edit` items aimed at a slot whose `component_level='tool'` (section-editor's regenerate-then-reassemble path) · `deploy_tool_action.go` (forks insert `content_data='{}'` and `rendered_html = template verbatim`) · any LLM-generated tool template that externalises UI copy as `{{.section_heading}}`, `{{.calculate_button_label}}`, … (31 such fields on `tool-ab-test-calculator`, 08-15) · `rerender_single_page_action.go` `sectionHasVisibleContent` (drops the slot as BLANK — the page then "assembles to nothing")
- **fires when:** you see a raw `{{.` tag on a served tool page and file a section-edit "to fix the raw tag". The editor re-renders the slot from template + `content_data`; with `{}` every field is empty, so the raw tag is GONE and so is every heading, label, placeholder and button caption — 13,284 chars of markup, **0 visible characters** (measured on `page_components 1a9efade…`). The bugs 178/253 floors measure class-attribute retention (13,284 chars of `class="abc-…"` survive), so they pass. The item's own reassembly then fails ("blank slots [tool-x]") and the handoff records "the edit landed, its reassembly failed" — which is TRUE and reads as half-success when it is a hollowed tool. The next `page_rerender` on that page fails the same way, for a reason that looks like the rerender's.
- **the check:** before AND after any editor pass on a tool slot, measure visible text, not tags: `SELECT length(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(rendered_html,'<style[^>]*>.*?</style>','','gis'),'<script[^>]*>.*?</script>','','gis'),'<[^>]+>','','g'),'\s|&[a-z#0-9]+;','','g')) FROM page_components WHERE id='<slot>'` — a tool with 0 is a shell whatever its byte length. And read the TEMPLATE's `{{.` census first (`regexp_matches(html_template,'\{\{\.([a-z_0-9]+)','g')`): a fork whose template names copy fields that `content_data` does not carry cannot be repaired by ANY re-render — it needs the copy supplied (framework, not by hand) or a rebuild. Recovery when it has already fired: the tool-deployer's verbatim template is still in `content_components.html_template`; the pre-edit `rendered_html` is NOT archived for these rows (no `page_component_history` row for the pair) — do not assume the trigger caught it.
- **relations:** bugs_open/286 (records the case; asks for a text-content floor beside the class-attr floor) · bugs 178/253 (the floors that pass) · MEMORY [[a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact]] · the lane NOTES entry "a failed section_edit may have half-applied … read the artefact in BOTH directions" — this is the direction it did not read
- **added:** 2026-08-16, webdesign_tool_rebuilds lane (found grading the ab-test rerender at the artefact: 47 raw tags served, 0 visible chars stored — the same page, two different failures, neither the one the queue reported)

## An agent seeded WITHOUT a `description` cannot be spawned, cannot receive a message, and is missing from the admin list — and the spawn failure looks exactly like the handshake flake

- **footprint:** `agent_definitions.description` · any `INSERT INTO agent_definitions` seed whose column list omits `description` · `spawn_actions.go getAgentDefinition` · `ai_actions.go loadAgentDefinitionForAction` · `generate_image_actions.go loadAgentDefinitionForImageAction` · `platform/messaging/processor.go` (definition resolver) · `internal/core-manager/admin/system_handlers.go` (agent list) · any orchestration that FAILED at a `spawn_agent` step
- **the trap:** the column is nullable with no default, and until commit `3c8a87101` all five readers scanned it into a plain Go `string`. A row with NULL description therefore fails EVERY path that loads it: `spawn_agent` dies with `sql: Scan error on column index 3, name "description": converting NULL to string is unsupported`; the messaging processor would fail the agent's first message the same way; the admin list `continue`s past the row so the agent silently vanishes from the one place a human would look. `[MEASURED 2026-08-16]` exactly one live definition was in this state — `brief-fidelity-auditor`, whose seed's column list simply omitted `description` — 1 of 193, the other 3 NULLs fleet-wide being inactive scratch probes. **The failure wears the spawn→call handshake flake's costume** (MEMORY: ~half of spawn→call pairs fail fleet-wide), so a session seeing `FAILED|spawn_<x>` will retry and move on. **Behind an `error_step` it is invisible**: the improvement loop's audit chain continues past a failed auditor by design, so a NULL-description auditor makes every sweep report COMPLETED with that auditor silently skipped.
- **the check, before you conclude a spawn "flaked":** read the error column, not the status — `SELECT left(error,200) FROM orchestration_states WHERE correlation_id='<corr>'`. `converting NULL to string` on `description` is this, not the flake. And before you seed ANY agent: `SELECT type FROM agent_definitions WHERE description IS NULL AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL;` must not list it after your seed applies — or just put `description` in the column list. `TestAgentDefinitionDescriptionIsNeverScannedBare` (`agent_definition_nullable_columns_test.go`) fails the build if a sixth bare reader appears; it is module-wide because two of the five were outside `actions`.
- **fix state:** data half LIVE (mig `420`, one row); code half (`COALESCE(description,'')` at all five readers) committed with `bugs_closed/290`, inert until the next chassis + core-manager roll. ~~`NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` on the column is the cleaner door and is the OWNER's call~~ **UPDATE 2026-08-16 (same day): the OWNER RULED for it — migration `438` APPLIED, `is_nullable=NO, default=''`, induced with a rolled-back probe insert.** So the trap is now CLOSED on every binary including today's: a seed that omits `description` gets `''`. What remains true is the READ side of this entry — if you ever add a sixth reader, COALESCE anyway (belt and braces; the test enforces it), and if you ever see `converting NULL to string` on this column again, the constraint has been dropped and that is the finding.
- **source:** 2026-08-16, `bugs_open/279` lane, the FIRST real spawn of `brief-fidelity-auditor` after migration `419` wired it into the improvement loop. Found because the lane was watching that exact orchestration for a different proof; the error string was read rather than the status retried.
- **relations:** `bugs_closed/290` · `bugs_closed/279` (the wiring that exposed it) · `bugs_closed/115` (the auditor "nobody ran" — two causes, not one) · MEMORY [[spawn-call-handshake-races]] (the flake this impersonates)
- **added:** 2026-08-16, bugs_open/279 lane

## `pages.sections` now carries LOCKED live slots that are NOT in `site_plan_sections` — a plan-vs-cache diff is not drift when the difference is a locked row, and a plan-only reader is not the whole page

- **footprint:** `pages.sections` · `site_plan_sections` · `page_components.locked_at`/`lock_type` · `load_page_sections_from_spec_action.go` · `discovery_checks/check_section_source_drift.go` · `datahelpers/locked_page_sections.go` (`LoadLockedPageSlots`, `MergeLockedPageSlots`) · any query that joins `pages.sections` against the current plan and calls a mismatch "drift"
- **the trap:** since commit `7d9b7334a` (bugs_open/285, the section-list-assembly case; register LOCK-008; Go — inert until the roll after it) the loader merges the page's non-agent-writable `page_components` rows into the list it assembles and writes THAT into `pages.sections`. So on any page carrying a human-locked section the plan does not name (13 fleet-wide on 2026-08-15: webdesign.uk/contact `chat-input-box`, 12 loancalculator.co.uk calculators under positional slots `tool-2`/`tool-3`/…), the authoritative table and the cache legitimately differ by exactly that section — and the next rebuild will KEEP it, not revert anything. A raw `orderedListsEqual(plan, cache)` reads that as drift; a raw "cache has a name the plan lacks ⇒ someone hand-edited the cache" reads it as a human edit. Both are wrong. The reverse trap too: a plan-only reader (`site_plan_sections` alone, or `PlanSpecifiedSectionCounts`' tier order) still does NOT see the locked section — the loader's merge does not propagate to the readers that re-implement the tier order (`page_section_satisfiability`, `ensure_page_section_layout`, `plan_section_counts`, `tool_content_item`, `flag_page_image_rebuild`, `check_sectionless_pages`, `check_literal_markdown` — named in the file header), so "the plan says the page has N sections" is N minus its locks.
- **the check:** before calling a plan-vs-cache difference drift, view BOTH sides through the loader's own merge — `datahelpers.MergeLockedPageSlots(list, locked)` with `locked` from `LoadLockedPageSlots(ForSite)` — exactly as `check_section_source_drift` now does; in SQL, subtract the page's locked slots first: `SELECT COALESCE(pc.slot_name,'') FROM page_components pc JOIN pages p ON p.id=pc.page_id WHERE p.site_id='<id>' AND p.name='<page>' AND NOT (pc.locked_at IS NULL OR (pc.lock_type='timed' AND pc.lock_expires_at IS NOT NULL AND pc.lock_expires_at < NOW()))`. And when a `lock_blocked_change … blocked_action=remove` item appears AFTER the roll that carries `7d9b7334a`, that is a REGRESSION signal, not the old noise — read `orchestration_states.collected_data->'spec_sections'->'locked_sections_merged'` for the run.
- **why it is a landmine and not just a note:** the fix's own first consequence would have been the noise it removed — `section_source_drift` is enabled live in the completeness-discovery-agent and would have filed one `needs_human_review` item per fixed page (13) on its next pass; it was changed in the same commit only because the consumer census found it. The next reader who writes a plan-vs-cache census (there have been several: 016b §9 "a one-source check of a two-source authority", `bugs_open/002` error C, migration 154) will hit it without a symptom.
- **source:** 2026-08-15/16, `bugfix_285_lock_blind_section_list` lane; `bugs_open/285_HANDOFF_2026-08-15_section_list_assembly_is_lock_blind_…`
- **relations:** LANDMINES "`pages.sections` is a materialised CACHE — the build reads `site_plan_sections`" (still true; the cache now also carries what the build ADDS) · "A completeness floor on `page_components` must exclude LOCKED slots" (the prune floor's `planned − locked` becomes exact under this fix) · "A `lock_blocked_change` item does NOT mean the copy differed" (an in-list locked section still draws an `overwrite` item per pass; only the `remove` items stop) · register LOCK-008, PLAN-029, PBP-035 · `bugs_closed/058`
- **added:** 2026-08-16, bugfix_285_lock_blind_section_list lane

## `jsonb::text IS DISTINCT FROM $1` against a Go-marshalled JSON string is ALWAYS true — the "guarded" UPDATE fires on every run and looks exactly like a working guard

- **footprint:** any `UPDATE … WHERE <jsonb column>::text IS DISTINCT FROM $1` (or `<>`/`=` on `::text`) where `$1` is produced by Go `json.Marshal` · `load_page_sections_from_spec_action.go` (three sites until `7d9b7334a`, one jsonb-compared sync after) · grep: `grep -rn "::text IS DISTINCT FROM\|::text <> \$\|::text = \$" platform/ --include=*.go`
- **the trap:** Postgres renders jsonb text with a space after every comma and colon (`["hero", "contact-info"]`, `{"a": 1}`); Go's `json.Marshal` renders none (`["hero","contact-info"]`, `{"a":1}`). The two strings never compare equal for any non-trivial value, so the guard's "only when changed" clause is dead: the row is rewritten and `updated_at` bumped on every execution, and nothing errors. Measured live 2026-08-15 on webdesign.uk/contact: `sections::text IS DISTINCT FROM '["hero","contact-info"]'` → **t**; `sections IS DISTINCT FROM '["hero","contact-info"]'::jsonb` → **f**. Every page-build had been bumping `pages.updated_at` since the guard was written (2026-07-06), so any reader using `pages.updated_at` as "the page's list changed" was reading build cadence.
- **the check:** compare as jsonb, never as text — `WHERE col IS DISTINCT FROM $1::jsonb` (jsonb equality is structural: key order and whitespace do not matter, array order does). If you must compare text, canonicalise BOTH sides in SQL (`col::text` vs `$1::jsonb::text`). Prove a guard is live by running the UPDATE twice and asserting the second reports 0 rows: `UPDATE … RETURNING 1` / `GET DIAGNOSTICS`, or read `xmax`/`updated_at` before and after — a guard you have never seen refuse is a guard you have not tested (RFC_006's induced-failure discipline).
- **source:** 2026-08-15, `bugfix_285_lock_blind_section_list` lane, found while consolidating the loader's three per-tier syncs into one
- **relations:** LANDMINES "`pages.sections` is a materialised CACHE" · register LOCK-008 (the fix that removed this instance) · MEMORY [[a-quiet-test-passes-when-the-rule-is-gone]] (a guard that cannot fail is a guard that is not there)
- **added:** 2026-08-16, bugfix_285_lock_blind_section_list lane

## A `*_TRIGGER_*` / `*_DISPATCH_*` / `*_SUBMIT_*` script has no dry-run and PUBLISHES on every invocation — re-running it "to see the output again" is a second dispatch, and the receipt looks like the first

- **footprint:** `fixloop_eg_dartsonline/097_TRIGGER_council_review_v1.sh` · `090_TRIGGER_needs_diagnosis_v1.sh` · `scripts/trigger-landmine-verifier.sh` · `scripts/initial_messages/**/0*_submit_*.sh` / `*_trigger_*.sh` · `staged_component_build/scripts/DISPATCH_s6_component_run.sh` · any script whose body ends in a `kcat -P` / kafka publish
- **fires when:** the first run scrolled (097 prints ~70 lines; the correlation block is at the TOP), you `tail`ed it, missed the id, and run the same command again through `grep`/`head` to read the head. Nothing in the second run says "already submitted": it prints a fresh run correlation, deletes its own kcat pod, and lists BOTH orchestrations in its queue-depth table as if that were normal load. **The habit that bites is a correct one for `SELECT`/`git log`/reports** — re-run to read differently — and a trigger's output is not a report, it is a side effect's receipt.
- **the tell:** two `council-gate` (or `needs_diagnosis`) orchestrations within a minute with the same `fix_correlation_id` / target, both `EXECUTING_STEP` in review seats — by which point they are already spending. `[MEASURED 2026-08-16]` `b5678c3a…` and `d1a20669…`, both `fix_correlation_id=75091072-…`, 26 s apart; not cancellable without hand-editing shared `orchestration_states` mid-LLM-step, for which there is no sanctioned procedure — so the round was paid twice.
- **the check:** run a trigger ONCE and capture its output to a file in the same breath — `./097_… sub.json 2>&1 | tee "$SCRATCH/council_$(date -u +%H%M).log"` — then read the file as many ways as you like. Before ANY re-run of a script with TRIGGER/DISPATCH/SUBMIT/PUBLISH in its name, query for the orchestration the first run made (097 prints the exact query; for 090, `site_work_items … item_type='needs_diagnosis' … created_at > now()-interval '10 minutes'`). CLAUDE.md already forbids the *latency* retry ("a missing orchestration row is almost always latency … do not retry on that evidence"); this is the same rule for the *I want to see the output again* case. Want a dry run? 097 has none — validate the JSON with `python3 -m json.tool` and count edits with `jq '.plan.edits|length'` instead.
- **source:** 2026-08-16, staged_component_build lane (RFC_029 revision round 2, submitted twice); WRONG_CALLS entry the same day
- **relations:** LANDMINES "A council run killed by a chassis roll looks exactly like a slow one for FOUR HOURS" (the other way a wait-for-verdict goes wrong) · CLAUDE.md "Council review of platform changes" (budget ~30 min, do not retry) · MEMORY [[kcat-publish-silently-drops]] (the opposite failure: exit 0 and NOTHING sent — the two together mean "count the orchestrations, never the exits")
- **added:** 2026-08-16, staged_component_build lane

## The site-facts relay answers **200 with `facts: []`** for a site whose `evidence_base` has an EMPTY facts array — a status-code probe for "does this site have facts" says yes, and every consumer that keys on the count refuses anyway

- **footprint:** `internal/core-manager/handlers/sitefacts.go` (`HandleGetSiteFacts`, predicate `ss.data ? 'facts'`) · `GET /api/v1/site-facts/:domain` · `site_specs.data->'facts'` where `aspect='evidence_base'` · `box/chat-service/facts.go` (`fetchFacts`, "returned zero facts") · `platform/orchestration/actions/tool_backend_provision.go` (`loadBackendEligibility`, `FactsCount`)
- **fires when:** you `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'` the relay (or read the handler's own header comment: "404: unknown domain, or the site has no current evidence_base row") to decide whether a site is ready for a facts-fed backend, and see 200. The handler gates on the KEY, not its length: a row carrying `"facts": []` (noted.co.uk, measured 2026-08-16 — 0 facts, `writer_block` 3,869 chars, 7 banned claims) is served as a normal 200 with an empty array. Every consumer then refuses on `len==0` — the chat binary will not start, TL-043's deploy gate refuses — so the site LOOKS ready at the relay and is not
- **the tell:** none at the status code. `journalctl -u sitechat@<domain>` says `facts relay returned zero facts` while your probe said 200; or a `backend_provision` item you expected is a deploy refusal naming `evidence_base facts`
- **the check:** never the status alone — read the count from the body: `curl -s -H "X-Facts-Token: $TOKEN" <relay>/<domain> | python3 -c 'import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(len(d.get("facts",[])))'` (0 = not ready, whatever the status), or the DB: `SELECT jsonb_array_length(ss.data->'facts') FROM site_specs ss JOIN sites s ON s.id=ss.site_id WHERE s.domain='<d>' AND ss.aspect='evidence_base' AND ss.is_current;`. A mechanism claim about a status code is a `curl` of the URL the claim is ABOUT, not a reading of the handler
- **source:** 2026-08-16, webdesign_uk_build_service lane — the claim "the relay 404s a site with no facts" was written into a Go error string, register TL-043 and a council rationale in one commit and refuted by the second-site proof run an hour later; WRONG_CALLS row the same day. No mis-build (every consumer reads the count), four corrections
- **relations:** register CHAT-010 (the relay) · TL-043 (the deploy gate that reads the count) · MEMORY [[a-print-statement-is-not-a-config-row]] (a claim about behaviour is not the behaviour) · WRONG_CALLS 2026-08-16
- **added:** 2026-08-16, webdesign_uk_build_service lane

## A `complete` work item's `result` may be the SPAWN RECORD, not the handler's reply — and since 2026-08-15 10:14Z that includes every 090 diagnosis item's "verdict"

- **footprint:** `site_work_items.result` for any item completed by a `loop` sub-workflow whose `complete_work_item` reads a sibling `output_field` un-suffixed — `build-dispatch-loop.process_item.mark_complete` (`"result": "handler_result"`), `diagnose-dispatch-loop` (same shape), `site-work-orchestrator.build_items_loop.complete_work_item` (`commit_sha: page_deployed`) · `prefixConfigStepReferences` (`coordinator.go:4443`, the `dataRefKeys` allow-list) · `CompleteWorkItemAction` → `datahelpers.ExtractActionInputs`/`GetMap("result")` · `090_TRIGGER_needs_diagnosis_v1.sh` readers
- **the trap:** the item says `complete` and its `result` is a well-formed JSON object — `{"role":"handler","topics":{…},"agent_id":…,"agent_type":"<handler>"}` — so a reader grades it, cites it, or takes it as the handler's self-report. It is `spawn_agent`'s output. The reply is at `handler_result_<iter>` on the PARENT orchestration; `mark_complete` asks for `handler_result` (un-suffixed, its config key `result` is not on the rewriter's allow-list), finds nothing, and the aggressive recursive search returns the spawn record. The WORK happened; the record of it did not. ~75% of dispatch-loop completions since the roll that fixed `bugs_closed/274` (before it, a different wrong payload sat in the same slot).
- **the tell:** `result ? 'topics' AND result ? 'agent_id'` and no `response` key. For a 090: the `needs_diagnosis` item's `result` names `diagnose-orchestrator` — that is not a verdict.
- **the check:** never read outcome from the item. Deploys → the URL/DB row/bucket. 090 verdicts → `SELECT collected_data->'verdict', collected_data->'route' FROM orchestration_states WHERE correlation_id='<RUN_CORRELATION_ID>' AND owner_agent_type='diagnose-agent'` (or `diagnosis_artifacts`). Census of the shape: `SELECT handler_agent, count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE status='complete' AND result ? 'topics' AND result ? 'agent_id' AND updated_at > now()-interval '1 day' GROUP BY 1;`
- **why it is a landmine and not just a note:** it fires with no symptom — the item is green, the JSON is valid, and the run it belongs to genuinely completed. The 090 that diagnosed this very bug completed with its own item in this shape while its verdict sat correctly on the diagnose-agent row; a session reading the item would have recorded "no verdict".
- **source:** 2026-08-16, mortgagecalculator adoption lane; `bugs_closed/290_HANDOFF_2026-08-16_dispatch_loop_completes_items_with_the_spawn_record_…` (the `spawn_record` slug — a sibling 287 exists) §9/§9a/§9b/§6a; 090 run `fb7ae3bc…` (REFUTED on the resolver's name only)
- **relations:** `bugs_closed/274` (whose fix exposed this) · `bugs_closed/213` §D (the previous foreign-payload shape) · `bugs_open/248` R1 (same aggressive search, `asset_id`) · MEMORY [[a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact]] · [[bugfix-287-item-result-is-the-spawn-record]] · LANDMINES "the two-strike rule" (a `complete` is a strike whatever it holds)
- **added:** 2026-08-16, mortgagecalculator adoption lane

## A `site_specs.<aspect>.<path>`-sourced field in `input_schema` is re-resolved from the ASPECT on every section rerender — a hand-edit to `page_components.content_data` reads back correctly, survives the gate, and is silently reverted by the very rerender you fire to publish it

- **footprint:** `content_components.input_schema` where `fields.*.source` matches `site_specs.*` (e.g. `case-studies-list.case_studies` → `site_specs.portfolio.case_studies`) · `page_components.content_data` on any page using such a component · `site_specs` rows with `aspect IN ('portfolio', …)` and `is_current` · `rerender_page_sections` (`reason=section_data_resolved`)
- **fires when:** you repair copy the way every leopardess/brochure recipe says to — `UPDATE page_components SET content_data=…`, run the two escalation-gate queries (both clean: the field is present and non-empty), fire ONE rerender, and verify at the served page. The `llm`-sourced slots on the same page carry your edits; the aspect-sourced field comes back as the aspect's value and `content_data` itself has been rewritten to match, so a re-read after the rerender says your edit was never made. Measured 2026-08-16 on leopardessconsulting.co.uk `/case-studies.html`: `case_studies[].results` edited 10:12Z, rerender 10:15Z COMPLETED, served text unchanged, `content_data` reverted to the aspect (`8869edfc`, is_current since 07-10); the `generic-text-block` (llm) edit in the same transaction went live. Fixed by editing the aspect and rerendering again.
- **the tell:** one slot's edit vanishes while its neighbours' survive AND `content_data` no longer contains it — same shape as the `static`-source entry above but the source of truth is another TABLE, so "author only the llm keys" is not enough advice: the llm keys were fine, the field you needed to change was never yours.
- **the check:** before editing any field, read its source: `SELECT k, cc.input_schema->'fields'->k->>'source' FROM content_components cc JOIN page_components pc ON pc.component_id=cc.id, jsonb_object_keys(cc.input_schema->'fields') k WHERE pc.page_id='<page>' AND pc.slot_name='<slot>';` — a value starting `site_specs.` names the aspect and json path to edit instead (`UPDATE site_specs SET data = jsonb_set(data, '{<path>,…}', …) WHERE site_id=… AND aspect='<aspect>' AND is_current`, back it up first — site rule), then rerender. Same lesson as `site_plan` being the section authority (`L9_services_carousels.sql` §3): **the aspect is the authority; `content_data` is a cache of it.**
- **source:** 2026-08-16, leopardess services-restore session (RUNNING_NOTES 2026-08-16); one wasted rerender
- **relations:** LANDMINES "A `static`-source field in a component's `input_schema` OVERWRITES your stored `content_data` on every section resolve" (the same trap for the other two source families — read them together) · "A queue `page_rerender` item with no `reason` … is ASSEMBLE-ONLY" (the opposite failure: nothing re-resolves) · `docs/leopardessconsulting/RUNBOOK.md` landmine 14 (a section-component fork does not survive rerender — same "the rerender re-derives from the authority" mechanism)
- **added:** 2026-08-16, leopardess services-restore session

### A census over `workflow.steps.*.action` is BLIND to every action nested in a `sub_workflow` — 80 live invocations, 19 action names, and the answer comes back well-formed and short

- **footprint:** `agent_definitions.default_config->'workflow'->'steps'` · any query of the form `jsonb_each(default_config->'workflow'->'steps')` reading `->>'action'` · `loop` steps · blast-radius and "who calls this action" measurements · council-gate footprint maps · deprecating or changing any registered action · `render_component`, `assemble_page`, `plan_sections`, `save_page_sections`, `call_agent`, `spawn_agent`, `create_work_item`, `complete_work_item`
- **fires when:** you answer "which live workflows execute action X?" — for a blast radius, a footprint, a deprecation, or a council submission's pipeline census — by iterating the top-level steps map and reading each step's `action`. **It returns a clean, plausible, non-empty answer, and it silently omits everything a loop runs.**
- **the mechanism, measured 2026-08-16:** a `loop` step carries an entire nested workflow at `config.sub_workflow.steps.<name>.action`. Fleet-wide, live and non-snapshot: **1,271 top-level steps, 18 of which carry a `sub_workflow`, hiding 80 action invocations across 19 distinct action names.** Note the near-miss shape too — `config ? 'action'` on a loop step returns **0**, so a census that *tries* to look inside the loop, but guesses the key one level too shallow, reports "no nested actions" and reads as a completed check.
- **the tell, and why you will not see it:** the top-level census is not empty, so nothing looks wrong. Caught here only because a **text control** disagreed with the structured query: `default_config::text LIKE '%render_component%'` found `page-content-writer` while `steps.*.action='render_component'` found **nothing at all** — i.e. a whole render path read as executed by no live workflow, which was false. Without the control I would have published "`render_component` is dormant" in a council submission.
- **the check:** run both and reconcile the difference before publishing either.
  ```sql
  -- structured (executes it), now including sub_workflows
  WITH s AS (SELECT ad.type, st.value AS step
             FROM agent_definitions ad, LATERAL jsonb_each(ad.default_config->'workflow'->'steps') st
             WHERE ad.is_active AND COALESCE(ad.is_snapshot,false)=false AND ad.deleted_at IS NULL)
  SELECT DISTINCT type FROM s WHERE step->>'action' = '<action>'
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT s.type FROM s, LATERAL jsonb_each(s.step->'config'->'sub_workflow'->'steps') sw
   WHERE sw.value->>'action' = '<action>';
  -- text control (mentions it) — the over-inclusive upper bound; a difference is a question, not noise
  SELECT type FROM agent_definitions WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false
    AND deleted_at IS NULL AND default_config::text LIKE '%<action>%';
  ```
  A text hit that the structured query misses is either a deeper nesting or a mere mention (a footprint map, a `next_step` label) — **open the row and look**, because those two have opposite meanings for a blast radius.
- **the general form:** a structured query encodes a belief about the document's SHAPE, and when the shape is wrong the query does not error — it answers a narrower question, correctly, in the same format as the question you asked. A text scan over the same column encodes no shape belief, which is exactly why it makes a usable control even though it over-reports.
- **relations:** MEMORY [[measurement-discipline-index]] (interrogating what doesn't EXIST returns a well-formed answer) · [[a-post-fix-zero-needs-a-demand-control]] (a zero needs a control that could have made it non-zero) · `bugs_open/283` §10 (the pipeline census this was found in) · the council `guardian` seat's standing objection that a Go-file census is not a pipeline census
- **source:** 2026-08-16, `bugfix_283_component_instance_scope` lane, answering the council `guardian` seat's round-2 objection that the plan's blast radius stopped at the Go-file level. Both counts read first-hand off the live DB; the `sub_workflow` key path was read out of `page-content-writer`'s own `process_sections_loop` config rather than guessed, after `config ? 'action'` returned 0 and the first guess proved wrong.
- **added:** 2026-08-16, bugfix_283 lane

### A component seed written in the JSON-Schema `input_schema` dialect is now REFUSED by the table — and the comment that told you the dialect was dead is the same comment that let four of them in

- **footprint:** `content_components.input_schema` · `chk_input_schema_no_legacy_dialect` · `docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/*component*.sql` (any component seed) · `datahelpers.SchemaContentFields` / `WarnLegacyDialect` / `IsLegacyInputSchemaDialect` · `store_generated_component_action.go`
- **fires when:** you write or re-run a component seed, restore a component from a `bak_*`/`component_versions` copy, or copy an existing seed as a template — and the schema you carry across has a top-level `"properties"` key. Since migration `437` (2026-08-16) the INSERT/UPDATE is refused: `ERROR … violates check constraint "chk_input_schema_no_legacy_dialect"`. Write `{"fields": {"<name>": {"source","required","type","llm_guidance",...}}}` instead. Nested `properties` under `fields.<x>.items` is the shape of an ITEM and is fine — only the top level is constrained.
- **why the wrong result used to look exactly like the right one:** the seed committed, the component rendered, and nothing said anything. `SchemaContentFields` *projects* the old dialect onto the new view, so readers kept working; the only signal was `WarnLegacyDialect`, a `Warn` line on `agent-chassis` that nobody reads. Four components were seeded that way over three weeks and none surfaced. Worse, the helper's own doc comment said the dialect was *"extinct fleet-wide (0 of 173 as at 2026-07-21)"* — a census that was true when written and false four days later, and a reader who trusted it specified a type gate that would have been blind to all four (`bugs_closed/265` §Defect 1).
- **⚠ the tripwire's meaning has INVERTED — do not debug it as a seed problem.** `WarnLegacyDialect` is now an `Error`, and it can no longer fire on a `content_components` row while the constraint stands. A firing means **the constraint is gone**, or the caller is reading a `bak_*`/`component_versions` copy, or an in-memory schema before a write. Check `SELECT conname FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname='chk_input_schema_no_legacy_dialect'` **first**; if it is present, the schema did not come from the live table.
- **the generalisable bit:** *a census in a comment is stale the day after it is taken, and it reads exactly like an invariant.* If you find yourself writing "0 of N as at <date>" as a licence for a downstream decision, the honest forms are a constraint (checkable at any moment) or a marked `[MEASURED <date>]` that a reader knows to re-run. The producer here was never the component-creator either — all four were hand SQL — so **read `created_from` / `source_agent_type` before you decide which seam to guard**; a gate on the agent would have caught none of them.
- **source:** `bugs_closed/265`; migration `437_content_components_refuse_legacy_input_schema_dialect.sql` (+ `_ROLLBACK`); register `CLC-015`; lane `docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_265_legacy_dialect_unrepresentable/`
- **added:** 2026-08-16, bugfix_265 lane


### Widening a planner's component MENU changes nothing on its own — `validate_site_plan` silently deletes every proposed name its own whitelist does not carry, and the deletion is invisible in the plan

- **footprint:** `loadComponentNameResolver` · `componentNameResolver.resolve` · `ValidateSitePlanAction` · `validate_site_plan` (the action) · `validate_components` / `menu_field` (its step config keys) · `agent_definitions` steps `load_components` / `load_available_components` · `content_components.component_level` · `site_plan_sections`
- **fires when:** you widen what a planner may be OFFERED — a new `component_level` in a menu query, a new opt-in flag on the menu (e.g. `plan_includes_tools`, migration 407), a `requires-backend` style gate (419), a new component class — and then judge the result by what the plan contains. It also fires the other way: when you debug a plan that is MISSING something and reach for "the LLM chose not to".
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** the planner really does propose the widened components (they are in `llm_call_log.response_text` and in `collected_data.llm_plan`), the step returns success, `write_site_plan` writes a perfectly well-formed plan, and `site_plan_sections` simply has fewer rows. The ONLY trace of the deletion is one `Warn` per name — `"ValidateSitePlanAction: dropped unresolvable section name"` — on a busy service whose startup lines have already scrolled. Measured (`bugs_open/282`, run corr `2f74a975`, 2026-08-15): menu offered 11 tool functions, the planner placed one on each of 12 pages, `collected_data.validate_plan` carried **zero** of them. Nobody noticed for a day, and the first diagnosis blamed the planner's judgement.
- **the check, BEFORE you conclude anything about a planner's choices:** read the three artefacts of the one run in order — they are all in the same row, and the drop sits between the second and the third.
  ```sql
  -- NB: the column is owner_agent_type, NOT agent_type (that error reads like a missing join)
  SELECT jsonb_array_length(collected_data->'available_components')                       AS offered,
         (SELECT jsonb_agg(p->'sections') FROM jsonb_array_elements(collected_data->'llm_plan'->'result'->'pages') p WHERE p->>'name'='index') AS proposed,
         (SELECT jsonb_agg(p->'sections') FROM jsonb_array_elements(collected_data->'validate_plan'->'pages') p       WHERE p->>'name'='index') AS accepted
    FROM orchestration_states WHERE correlation_id = '<the run>';
  ```
  `offered` >> `accepted` with `proposed` in between means the acceptance surface ate it. Since 2026-08-16 the fix has a positive tell too: `grep "resolved via the planner's menu"` in the chassis logs says the menu arm fired, which is the only thing that distinguishes "the widening works" from "the planner proposed nothing from the widened class this time".
- **⚠ the offer and the acceptance live in DIFFERENT LANGUAGES, and only one of them is in this repo.** The menu is a SQL string inside `agent_definitions.default_config` (live on apply, editable by any migration); the acceptance is Go (inert until an image rolls). So a menu widening cannot be reviewed by reading the Go, a resolver change cannot be reviewed by reading the migrations, and the two halves can never ship simultaneously. **Fix a widening by naming the menu, not by copying its predicate:** `menu_field` on the `validate_plan` step (migration `439`) makes validate accept the rows the planner was actually shown. Copying the predicate into Go would be a third hand-maintained copy — 407's text had already drifted by the time 282 was filed, because 419 edited the same query.
- **⚠ do NOT "fix the inconsistency" by widening `loadComponentNameResolver` itself.** Three of its four call sites are `apply_gap_plan_action.go` (content-gap-planner, 131 dispatches/30d), whose menu 407 and register PLAN-049 record as **deliberately** not widened — "gap-planning a NEW tool page is a different authority". A resolver-level widening hands that path an authority an owner-facing decision withheld, silently and with no config to show for it.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/282` · register `PLAN-027` (the resolver) + `PLAN-049` (the 407 menu widening) · migrations `407` / `419` / `439` · `016b` §9 (offer-vs-accept pattern) · MEMORY [[writes-the-field-is-not-reads-the-field]] · [[a-post-fix-zero-needs-a-demand-control]]
- **source:** `bugs_open/282`, fixed 2026-08-16 (`5534e9f71`); lane `docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_282_validate_accepts_menu/`
- **added:** 2026-08-16, bugfix_282 lane

### The `git mv` copy-not-move landmine has FIRED — twice, live, for a fortnight — and there is now a check, because reading the stale copy is how you lose a day

- **footprint:** `bugs_open/` · `bugs_closed/` · `git mv` · `scripts/pattern-check.py` (`check_bug_file_duplicated`) · any commit closing a bug
- **fires when:** you close a bug with `git mv` and then commit naming only ONE of the two paths (the pathspec rule tells you to be narrow, and being narrow is exactly what drops the deletion). The bug then exists in **both** directories. Measured 2026-08-16: `145` (closed 2026-07-31, live-verified v1.0.1217) and `072` (closed 2026-07-31) had both been sitting in `bugs_open/` ever since — the open backlog overstated itself by two for a fortnight.
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** `ls bugs_closed/` shows your file, `git status` is clean, and the commit's scope block lists what you expected. Nothing anywhere says *the old path is still tracked*. The existing landmine for this told you to verify at HEAD; both of these were closed **after** that entry was written, so "there is a landmine" was not enough.
- **the cost, which is not cosmetic:** a session picking "the next unowned open bug" reads the stale copy — still headed OPEN, still carrying the old close criteria — and redoes finished work. That is how this was found: a lane verified `145`'s fix at the pod, with controls, before discovering it had been closed a fortnight earlier at `v1.0.1217`. **And the duplicate splits the record**: `072`'s open copy accumulated a re-verification on a second image and a measured correction ("buys 5 sites" → **buys ONE PAGE**) that its closed copy never received, so whichever copy you read, you read an incomplete history.
- **the check (new, and induced on its own motivating case):** `scripts/pattern-check.py`'s `check_bug_file_duplicated` fires on any commit touching either directory when a basename exists in both. Proven by auditing `a4bf9f1e9` — the very commit that created the `145` duplicate — which now reports it, with a control commit touching neither directory staying silent. Advisory, like the rest of that file.
- **if you find one: do NOT just delete the loser.** Diff first, with the unwrap trick (`tr '\n' ' ' < f | tr -s ' ' | grep -c "…"`) because these files are hard-wrapped and a line-oriented grep reports false absences. `072`'s stale copy held 95 unique lines. Carry anything unique into the survivor, attributed and marked as history, *then* remove the path.
- **source:** 2026-08-16, `bugfix_265_legacy_dialect_unrepresentable` lane, found while verifying `145` against the fresh `v1.0.1304` roll; recovery recorded in `bugs_closed/072_…contact_info…md` §RECOVERED
- **added:** 2026-08-16, bugfix_265 lane


### ~~ADDENDUM: the platform's OWN code does the normalisation that entry tells checkers never to do~~ **RESOLVED 2026-08-18 — the five mechanisms are now CORRECT, not merely consistent**

> **CORRECTED 2026-08-18.** The five DB-derived mechanisms below collapse `/x/` and
> `/x/index.html` via `NormalizePagePath`. That made them WRONG on the B2 route and right on
> the git route. With `worker.js` now serving both forms everywhere (**DGH-012**), the
> collapsing is accurate on both routes and **`NormalizePagePath` was deliberately left
> untouched** — fixing the route was the cheaper, more complete fix, and four of its five
> consumers are build-time where the route is not in hand. **What still stands:** the
> footprint list, and the general lesson that five mechanisms sharing one definition agree
> with each other whether or not they are right about the world. **What is dead:** the
> census, the "one link of live damage", and the fix suggestion — it is done.


- **footprint:** `datahelpers.NormalizePagePath` · `datahelpers.PageURLSet` / `NewPageURLSet` / `Contains` (`platform/orchestration/datahelpers/links.go:215-227`, `399-411`) · `loadResolverPageSet` (`resolve_internal_links_action.go`) · `validate_page_content.go` · `datahelpers.RepairPageLinks` (`link_repair.go`) · `check_phantom_internal_links.go` · `nav_tables.go:loadFetchablePageSet` · `sites.github_repo`
- **read the earlier entry first** — search this file for *"A `/section/` URL 404s on every B2-hosted site, and a local server hides it"*. It owns the root property, the worker lines and the fleet confirmation (`mortgagecalculator.co.uk/guides/` is already in its list). **This is not a second bug.** It is the half that bites when you are reading the platform's own verdicts instead of probing URLs — and it was found independently on 2026-08-16 by a lane that grepped this file for *"trailing slash"* and *"directory-form"* and missed the existing entry, which is phrased *"a `/section/` URL"*. **Grep this file by FOOTPRINT SYMBOL (`worker.js`, `NormalizePagePath`), not by the words you would use for the symptom** — the same lesson MEMORY records as [[grep-landmines-for-your-symbols]].
- **what the earlier entry does not say:** its closing warning is *"if a checker disagrees with production, change the checker to match production — never the reverse."* **Production already disagrees with production.** `NormalizePagePath` strips `index.html` and then trailing `/`, so `/tools/x/` and `/tools/x/index.html` collapse to one key and `PageURLSet.Contains` returns **true** for the form the worker 404s. That set is shared deliberately — its own comment requires the gate and the audit to agree "by one literal implementation" — so the build-time resolver EMITS the dead form, the deploy gate PASSES it, `RepairPageLinks` leaves it, `check_phantom_internal_links` calls it neither phantom nor unbuilt, and `loadFetchablePageSet` counts it fetchable. **Five mechanisms, one definition, all agreeing — which is normally the argument that an answer is trustworthy.**
- **it is ROUTE-dependent, which "every B2-hosted site" leaves implicit:** the git route serves BOTH forms — [MEASURED 2026-08-16] `relojistas.com/noticias/` **200** and `/noticias/index.html` **200** (`sites.github_repo='vm-sites'`) — against `mortgagecalculator.co.uk` `/guides/` `/about/` `/tools/repayment/` `/investor/` all **404** with every `…/index.html` 200 (`github_repo=''`), same on `gaswholesalers.com` and `leopardessconsulting.co.uk`. So the same href is a defect or not depending on a column none of the five mechanisms reads, and **the platform demonstrably can serve it right — on one of its two routes.**
- **the check, when a DB-derived mechanism tells you a link is fine:** probe the href **exactly as authored**; never tidy it into `index.html` shape first, because that rewrite IS the bug performed by hand. Fleet census of live exposure (**2** such hrefs on 2026-08-16, one per route, so live damage was one link):
  ```sql
  SELECT s.domain, p.url AS on_page, (regexp_matches(pc.rendered_html,'href="(/[^"]*/)"','g'))[1] AS href
    FROM page_components pc JOIN pages p ON p.id=pc.page_id JOIN sites s ON s.id=p.site_id
   WHERE pc.rendered_html IS NOT NULL AND p.deployed_at IS NOT NULL;   -- discard href='/'
  ```
- **the one check that DOES see it is `dead_internal_link_live`** (`check_site_structural_validity.go`) — it probes each href as written instead of deriving a verdict. It lives in `completeness-discovery-agent`, whose rotation `site-discovery-rotation-completeness` has been **`enabled=false` since 2026-08-10 17:40Z**. Do not read "no findings from that agent" as "no dead links".
- **⚠ do NOT fix this by making `NormalizePagePath` route-aware** — four of its five consumers are build-time, where the route is not in hand, and it exists precisely to keep gate and audit identical. **The fix is three lines in the worker**, and it is the rewrite the git route already does for free: `worker.js:9-12` special-cases only the root (`if (path === '/' || path === '') path = '/index.html';`); an `else if (path.endsWith('/')) path += 'index.html';` closes the class for human, external and inbound links too, not just internal ones. ⚠ **Shared serving across 36 zones: owner + council, not a lane's call**, and `scripts/cloudflare/README.md`'s warning applies — an update without the two B2 bindings strips the worker's credentials and takes every site down.
